div.head: Dramatis Personae

castList.castItem: George PAGE, a Gentleman dwelling at Windsor
MISTRESS ANNE PAGE, her daughter, in love with Fenton
WILLIAM PAGE, a boy, son to Page
Frank FORD, a Gentleman dwelling at Windsor
SIR HUGH EVANS, a Welsh parson
MISTRESS QUICKLY, servant to Doctor Caius
John RUGBY, servant to Doctor Caius

div.head: ACT I
SCENE I. Windsor. Before Page’s house
div.stage: Enter Justice Shallow, Slender and Sir Hugh Evans.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Sir Hugh, persuade me not. I will make a Star Chamber matter of it. If he were twenty Sir John Falstaffs, he shall not abuse Robert Shallow, esquire.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: In the county of Gloucester, Justice of Peace and Coram.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Ay, cousin Slender, and Custalorum.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, and Ratolorum too; and a gentleman born, Master Parson, who writes himself “Armigero” in any bill, warrant, quittance, or obligation—“Armigero.”

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Ay, that I do, and have done any time these three hundred years.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: All his successors, gone before him hath done’t; and all his ancestors that come after him may. They may give the dozen white luces in their coat.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: It is an old coat.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: The dozen white louses do become an old coat well. It agrees well, passant. It is a familiar beast to man, and signifies love.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: The luce is the fresh fish. The salt fish is an old coat.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I may quarter, coz.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: You may, by marrying.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: It is marring indeed, if he quarter it.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Not a whit.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Yes, py’r Lady. If he has a quarter of your coat, there is but three skirts for yourself, in my simple conjectures. But that is all one. If Sir John Falstaff have committed disparagements unto you, I am of the Church, and will be glad to do my benevolence to make atonements and compremises between you.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: The Council shall hear it; it is a riot.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: It is not meet the Council hear a riot. There is no fear of Got in a riot. The Council, look you, shall desire to hear the fear of Got, and not to hear a riot. Take your vizaments in that.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Ha! O’ my life, if I were young again, the sword should end it.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: It is petter that friends is the sword, and end it; and there is also another device in my prain, which peradventure prings goot discretions with it. There is Anne Page, which is daughter to Master George Page, which is pretty virginity.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Mistress Anne Page? She has brown hair, and speaks small like a woman?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: It is that fery person for all the ’orld, as just as you will desire, and seven hundred pounds of moneys, and gold, and silver, is her grandsire upon his death’s-bed—Got deliver to a joyful resurrections!—give, when she is able to overtake seventeen years old. It were a goot motion if we leave our pribbles and prabbles, and desire a marriage between Master Abraham and Mistress Anne Page.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Did her grandsire leave her seven hundred pound?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Ay, and her father is make her a petter penny.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: I know the young gentlewoman; she has good gifts.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Seven hundred pounds, and possibilities, is goot gifts.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Well, let us see honest Master Page. Is Falstaff there?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Shall I tell you a lie? I do despise a liar as I do despise one that is false, or as I despise one that is not true. The knight Sir John is there, and I beseech you be ruled by your well-willers. I will peat the door for Master Page.

div.p: What, ho! Got pless your house here!

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Within. Who’s there?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Here is Got’s plessing, and your friend, and Justice Shallow, and here young Master Slender, that peradventures shall tell you another tale, if matters grow to your likings.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: I am glad to see your worships well. I thank you for my venison, Master Shallow.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Master Page, I am glad to see you, much good do it your good heart! I wished your venison better; it was ill killed. How doth good Mistress Page? And I thank you always with my heart, la, with my heart.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Sir, I thank you.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Sir, I thank you; by yea and no, I do.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: I am glad to see you, good Master Slender.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: How does your fallow greyhound, sir? I heard say he was outrun on Cotsall.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: It could not be judged, sir.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: You’ll not confess, you’ll not confess.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: That he will not. ’Tis your fault; ’tis your fault. ’Tis a good dog.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: A cur, sir.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Sir, he’s a good dog, and a fair dog, can there be more said? He is good, and fair. Is Sir John Falstaff here?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Sir, he is within; and I would I could do a good office between you.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: It is spoke as a Christians ought to speak.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: He hath wronged me, Master Page.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Sir, he doth in some sort confess it.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: If it be confessed, it is not redressed. Is not that so, Master Page? He hath wronged me, indeed he hath, at a word, he hath. Believe me. Robert Shallow, esquire, saith he is wronged.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Here comes Sir John.

div.stage: Enter Sir John Falstaff, Bardolph, Nym and Pistol.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Now, Master Shallow, you’ll complain of me to the King?

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Knight, you have beaten my men, killed my deer, and broke open my lodge.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: But not kissed your keeper’s daughter!

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Tut, a pin! This shall be answered.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I will answer it straight: I have done all this. That is now answered.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: The Council shall know this.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: ’Twere better for you if it were known in counsel: you’ll be laughed at.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Pauca verba, Sir John; goot worts.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Good worts? Good cabbage!—Slender, I broke your head. What matter have you against me?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Marry, sir, I have matter in my head against you, and against your cony-catching rascals, Bardolph, Nym, and Pistol. They carried me to the tavern and made me drunk, and afterwards picked my pocket.

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: You Banbury cheese!

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, it is no matter.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: How now, Mephostophilus?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, it is no matter.

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: Slice, I say! Pauca, pauca, slice, that’s my humour.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Where’s Simple, my man? Can you tell, cousin?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Peace, I pray you. Now let us understand; there is three umpires in this matter, as I understand: that is, Master Page, fidelicet Master Page; and there is myself, fidelicet myself; and the three party is, lastly and finally, mine host of the Garter.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: We three to hear it and end it between them.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Fery goot. I will make a prief of it in my notebook, and we will afterwards ’ork upon the cause with as great discreetly as we can.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Pistol!

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: He hears with ears.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: The tevil and his tam! What phrase is this, “He hears with ear”? Why, it is affectations.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Pistol, did you pick Master Slender’s purse?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, by these gloves, did he, or I would I might never come in mine own great chamber again else! Of seven groats in mill-sixpences, and two Edward shovel-boards that cost me two shilling and two pence a-piece of Yed Miller, by these gloves.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Is this true, Pistol?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: No, it is false, if it is a pick-purse.

lg.l: Ha, thou mountain-foreigner!—Sir John and master mine,
I combat challenge of this latten bilbo.—
Word of denial in thy labras here!
Word of denial! Froth and scum, thou liest.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Points at Nym. By these gloves, then, ’twas he.

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: Be avised, sir, and pass good humours. I will say “marry trap with you”, if you run the nuthook’s humour on me. That is the very note of it.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: By this hat, then, he in the red face had it. For though I cannot remember what I did when you made me drunk, yet I am not altogether an ass.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: What say you, Scarlet and John?

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Why, sir, for my part, I say the gentleman had drunk himself out of his five sentences.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: It is his “five senses”. Fie, what the ignorance is!

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: And being fap, sir, was, as they say, cashiered; and so conclusions passed the careers.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, you spake in Latin then too; but ’tis no matter. I’ll ne’er be drunk whilst I live again, but in honest, civil, godly company, for this trick. If I be drunk, I’ll be drunk with those that have the fear of God, and not with drunken knaves.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: So Got ’udge me, that is a virtuous mind.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: You hear all these matters denied, gentlemen; you hear it.

div.stage: Enter Mistress Ford, Mistress Page and her daughter Anne Page with wine.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Nay, daughter, carry the wine in, we’ll drink within.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: O heaven, this is Mistress Anne Page.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: How now, Mistress Ford?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Mistress Ford, by my troth, you are very well met. By your leave, good mistress.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Wife, bid these gentlemen welcome. Come, we have a hot venison pasty to dinner. Come, gentlemen, I hope we shall drink down all unkindness.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I had rather than forty shillings I had my book of Songs and Sonnets here.

div.p: How now, Simple, where have you been? I must wait on myself, must I? You have not the Book of Riddles about you, have you?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Book of Riddles? Why, did you not lend it to Alice Shortcake upon Allhallowmas last, a fortnight afore Michaelmas?

div.stage: Enter Shallow and Sir Hugh Evans.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Come, coz; come, coz, we stay for you. A word with you, coz. Marry, this, coz: there is, as ’twere, a tender, a kind of tender, made afar off by Sir Hugh here. Do you understand me?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, sir, you shall find me reasonable. If it be so, I shall do that that is reason.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Nay, but understand me.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: So I do, sir.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Give ear to his motions, Master Slender. I will description the matter to you, if you be capacity of it.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Nay, I will do as my cousin Shallow says. I pray you pardon me, he’s a Justice of Peace in his country, simple though I stand here.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: But that is not the question. The question is concerning your marriage.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Ay, there’s the point, sir.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Marry, is it; the very point of it—to Mistress Anne Page.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Why, if it be so, I will marry her upon any reasonable demands.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: But can you affection the ’oman? Let us command to know that of your mouth, or of your lips; for divers philosophers hold that the lips is parcel of the mouth. Therefore, precisely, can you carry your good will to the maid?

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Cousin Abraham Slender, can you love her?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I hope, sir, I will do as it shall become one that would do reason.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Nay, Got’s lords and his ladies! You must speak possitable, if you can carry her your desires towards her.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: That you must. Will you, upon good dowry, marry her?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I will do a greater thing than that, upon your request, cousin, in any reason.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Nay, conceive me, conceive me, sweet coz. What I do is to pleasure you, coz. Can you love the maid?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I will marry her, sir, at your request. But if there be no great love in the beginning, yet heaven may decrease it upon better acquaintance, when we are married and have more occasion to know one another. I hope upon familiarity will grow more contempt. But if you say “Marry her,” I will marry her. That I am freely dissolved, and dissolutely.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: It is a fery discretion answer, save the fall is in the ’ord “dissolutely.” The ’ort is, according to our meaning, “resolutely.” His meaning is good.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Ay, I think my cousin meant well.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, or else I would I might be hanged, la!

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Here comes fair Mistress Anne.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Here comes fair Mistress Anne.—Would I were young for your sake, Mistress Anne.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: The dinner is on the table, my father desires your worships’ company.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: I will wait on him, fair Mistress Anne.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: ’Od’s plessed will! I will not be absence at the grace.

div.stage: Exeunt Shallow and Sir Hugh Evans.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: Will’t please your worship to come in, sir?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: No, I thank you, forsooth, heartily; I am very well.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: The dinner attends you, sir.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I am not a-hungry, I thank you, forsooth. To Simple. Go, sirrah, for all you are my man, go wait upon my cousin Shallow.

div.p: A Justice of Peace sometime may be beholding to his friend for a man. I keep but three men and a boy yet, till my mother be dead. But what though? Yet I live like a poor gentleman born.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: I may not go in without your worship. They will not sit till you come.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I’ faith, I’ll eat nothing. I thank you as much as though I did.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: I pray you, sir, walk in.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I had rather walk here, I thank you. I bruised my shin th’ other day with playing at sword and dagger with a master of fence—three veneys for a dish of stewed prunes—and, by my troth, I cannot abide the smell of hot meat since. Why do your dogs bark so? Be there bears i’ the town?

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: I think there are, sir; I heard them talked of.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I love the sport well, but I shall as soon quarrel at it as any man in England. You are afraid, if you see the bear loose, are you not?

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: Ay, indeed, sir.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: That’s meat and drink to me now. I have seen Sackerson loose twenty times, and have taken him by the chain. But, I warrant you, the women have so cried and shrieked at it that it passed. But women, indeed, cannot abide ’em; they are very ill-favoured rough things.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Come, gentle Master Slender, come. We stay for you.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I’ll eat nothing, I thank you, sir.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: By cock and pie, you shall not choose, sir! Come, come.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Nay, pray you lead the way.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Come on, sir.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Mistress Anne, yourself shall go first.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: Not I, sir; pray you keep on.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Truly, I will not go first; truly, la! I will not do you that wrong.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: I pray you, sir.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I’ll rather be unmannerly than troublesome. You do yourself wrong, indeed, la!

div.head: SCENE II. The same
div.stage: Enter Sir Hugh Evans and Simple.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Go your ways, and ask of Doctor Caius’ house which is the way. And there dwells one Mistress Quickly, which is in the manner of his nurse, or his dry nurse, or his cook, or his laundry, his washer and his wringer.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Well, sir.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Nay, it is petter yet. Give her this letter. For it is a ’oman that altogether’s acquaintance with Mistress Anne Page; and the letter is to desire and require her to solicit your master’s desires to Mistress Anne Page. I pray you be gone. I will make an end of my dinner; there’s pippins and cheese to come.

div.head: SCENE III. A room in the Garter Inn
div.stage: Enter Falstaff, Host, Bardolph, Nym, Pistol and Robin.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Mine host of the Garter!

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: What says my bully rook? Speak scholarly and wisely.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Truly, mine host, I must turn away some of my followers.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Discard, bully Hercules; cashier. Let them wag; trot, trot.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I sit at ten pounds a week.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Thou’rt an emperor—Caesar, Keiser, and Pheazar. I will entertain Bardolph. He shall draw, he shall tap. Said I well, bully Hector?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Do so, good mine host.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: I have spoke, let him follow.—Let me see thee froth and lime. I am at a word, follow.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Bardolph, follow him. A tapster is a good trade. An old cloak makes a new jerkin; a withered servingman a fresh tapster. Go, adieu.

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: It is a life that I have desired. I will thrive.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: O base Hungarian wight, wilt thou the spigot wield?

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: He was gotten in drink. Is not the humour conceited?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I am glad I am so acquit of this tinderbox. His thefts were too open. His filching was like an unskilful singer, he kept not time.

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: The good humour is to steal at a minute’s rest.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: “Convey,” the wise it call. “Steal?” Foh! A fico for the phrase!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Well, sirs, I am almost out at heels.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: Why, then, let kibes ensue.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: There is no remedy, I must cony-catch, I must shift.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: Young ravens must have food.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Which of you know Ford of this town?

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: I ken the wight, he is of substance good.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: My honest lads, I will tell you what I am about.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: Two yards, and more.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: No quips now, Pistol. Indeed, I am in the waist two yards about, but I am now about no waste; I am about thrift. Briefly, I do mean to make love to Ford’s wife. I spy entertainment in her. She discourses, she carves, she gives the leer of invitation. I can construe the action of her familiar style; and the hardest voice of her behaviour, to be Englished rightly, is “I am Sir John Falstaff’s.”

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: He hath studied her will and translated her will—out of honesty into English.

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: The anchor is deep. Will that humour pass?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Now, the report goes she has all the rule of her husband’s purse. He hath a legion of angels.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: As many devils entertain, and “To her, boy,” say I.

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: The humour rises; it is good. Humour me the angels.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I have writ me here a letter to her; and here another to Page’s wife, who even now gave me good eyes too, examined my parts with most judicious oeillades. Sometimes the beam of her view gilded my foot, sometimes my portly belly.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: Then did the sun on dunghill shine.

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: I thank thee for that humour.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: O, she did so course o’er my exteriors with such a greedy intention that the appetite of her eye did seem to scorch me up like a burning-glass. Here’s another letter to her. She bears the purse too; she is a region in Guiana, all gold and bounty. I will be cheaters to them both, and they shall be exchequers to me; they shall be my East and West Indies, and I will trade to them both. Go, bear thou this letter to Mistress Page;—and thou this to Mistress Ford. We will thrive, lads, we will thrive.

lg.l: Shall I Sir Pandarus of Troy become,
And by my side wear steel? Then Lucifer take all!

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: I will run no base humour. Here, take the humour-letter. I will keep the ’haviour of reputation.

lg.l: To Robin. Hold, sirrah, bear you these letters tightly;
Sail like my pinnace to these golden shores.—
Rogues, hence, avaunt! Vanish like hailstones, go!
Trudge, plod away o’ th’ hoof, seek shelter, pack!
Falstaff will learn the humour of this age:
French thrift, you rogues—myself and skirted page.
Let vultures gripe thy guts! For gourd and fullam holds,
And high and low beguile the rich and poor.
Tester I’ll have in pouch when thou shalt lack,
Base Phrygian Turk!

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: I have operations in my head which be humours of revenge.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: Wilt thou revenge?

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: By welkin and her star!

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: With wit or steel?

lg.l: With both the humours, I.
I will discuss the humour of this love to Ford.
And I to Page shall eke unfold
How Falstaff, varlet vile,
His dove will prove, his gold will hold,
And his soft couch defile.

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: My humour shall not cool. I will incense Ford to deal with poison, I will possess him with yellowness, for the revolt of mine is dangerous. That is my true humour.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: Thou art the Mars of malcontents. I second thee. Troop on.

div.head: SCENE IV. A room in Doctor Caius’s house

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: What, John Rugby!

div.p: I pray thee go to the casement, and see if you can see my master, Master Doctor Caius, coming. If he do, i’ faith, and find anybody in the house, here will be an old abusing of God’s patience and the King’s English.

sp.speaker: RUGBY
sp.p: I’ll go watch.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Go; and we’ll have a posset for’t soon at night, in faith, at the latter end of a sea-coal fire.

div.p: An honest, willing, kind fellow, as ever servant shall come in house withal; and, I warrant you, no tell-tale nor no breed-bate. His worst fault is that he is given to prayer; he is something peevish that way, but nobody but has his fault. But let that pass. Peter Simple you say your name is?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Ay, for fault of a better.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: And Master Slender’s your master?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Ay, forsooth.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Does he not wear a great round beard, like a glover’s paring-knife?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: No, forsooth, he hath but a little wee face, with a little yellow beard, a Cain-coloured beard.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: A softly-sprighted man, is he not?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Ay, forsooth. But he is as tall a man of his hands as any is between this and his head. He hath fought with a warrener.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: How say you? O, I should remember him. Does he not hold up his head, as it were, and strut in his gait?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Yes, indeed, does he.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Well, heaven send Anne Page no worse fortune! Tell Master Parson Evans I will do what I can for your master. Anne is a good girl, and I wish—

sp.speaker: RUGBY
sp.p: Out, alas! Here comes my master.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: We shall all be shent. Run in here, good young man, go into this closet. He will not stay long.

div.p: What, John Rugby! John! What, John, I say! Go, John, go inquire for my master. I doubt he be not well, that he comes not home.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Vat is you sing? I do not like dese toys. Pray you, go and vetch me in my closet une boîtine verte, a box, a green-a box. Do intend vat I speak? A green-a box.

lg.l: Ay, forsooth, I’ll fetch it you.
Aside. I am glad he went not in himself. If he had found the young man, he would have been horn-mad.

p.emph: Fe, fe, fe fe! Ma foi, il fait fort chaud. Je m’en vais à la cour—la grande affaire.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Is it this, sir?

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Oui, mette-le au mon pocket. Dépêche, quickly—Vere is dat knave Rugby?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: What, John Rugby, John!

sp.speaker: RUGBY
sp.p: Here, sir.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: You are John Rugby, and you are Jack Rugby. Come, take-a your rapier, and come after my heel to the court.

sp.speaker: RUGBY
sp.p: ’Tis ready, sir, here in the porch.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By my trot, I tarry too long. ’Od’s me! Qu’ay j’oublié? Dere is some simples in my closet dat I vill not for the varld I shall leave behind.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Ay me, he’ll find the young man there, and be mad!

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: O diable, diable! Vat is in my closet? Villainy! Larron! Pulling Simple out. Rugby, my rapier!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Good master, be content.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Wherefore shall I be content-a?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: The young man is an honest man.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: What shall de honest man do in my closet? Dere is no honest man dat shall come in my closet.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: I beseech you, be not so phlegmatic. Hear the truth of it. He came of an errand to me from Parson Hugh.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Vell?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Ay, forsooth, to desire her to—

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Peace, I pray you.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Peace-a your tongue!—Speak-a your tale.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: To desire this honest gentlewoman, your maid, to speak a good word to Mistress Anne Page for my master in the way of marriage.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: This is all, indeed, la! But I’ll ne’er put my finger in the fire, and need not.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Sir Hugh send-a you?—Rugby, baille me some paper.—Tarry you a little-a while.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Aside to Simple. I am glad he is so quiet. If he had been throughly moved, you should have heard him so loud and so melancholy. But notwithstanding, man, I’ll do you your master what good I can; and the very yea and the no is, the French doctor, my master—I may call him my master, look you, for I keep his house, and I wash, wring, brew, bake, scour, dress meat and drink, make the beds, and do all myself—

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Aside to Mistress Quickly. ’Tis a great charge to come under one body’s hand.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Aside to Simple. Are you avised o’ that? You shall find it a great charge, and to be up early and down late; but notwithstanding—to tell you in your ear, I would have no words of it—my master himself is in love with Mistress Anne Page; but notwithstanding that, I know Anne’s mind. That’s neither here nor there.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: You jack’nape, give-a dis letter to Sir Hugh. By gar, it is a shallenge. I will cut his troat in de park, and I will teach a scurvy jackanape priest to meddle or make. You may be gone, it is not good you tarry here.—By gar, I will cut all his two stones. By gar, he shall not have a stone to throw at his dog.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Alas, he speaks but for his friend.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: It is no matter-a ver dat. Do not you tell-a me dat I shall have Anne Page for myself? By gar, I vill kill de Jack priest; and I have appointed mine host of de Jarteer to measure our weapon. By gar, I will myself have Anne Page.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Sir, the maid loves you, and all shall be well. We must give folks leave to prate. What, the good-year!

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Rugby, come to the court with me. To Mistress Quickly. By gar, if I have not Anne Page, I shall turn your head out of my door.—Follow my heels, Rugby.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: You shall have An—fool’s head of your own. No, I know Anne’s mind for that. Never a woman in Windsor knows more of Anne’s mind than I do, nor can do more than I do with her, I thank heaven.

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: Within. Who’s within there, ho?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Who’s there, I trow? Come near the house, I pray you.

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: How now, good woman? How dost thou?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: The better, that it pleases your good worship to ask.

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: What news? How does pretty Mistress Anne?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: In truth, sir, and she is pretty, and honest, and gentle; and one that is your friend, I can tell you that by the way, I praise heaven for it.

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: Shall I do any good, think’st thou? Shall I not lose my suit?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Troth, sir, all is in His hands above. But notwithstanding, Master Fenton, I’ll be sworn on a book she loves you. Have not your worship a wart above your eye?

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: Yes, marry, have I; what of that?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Well, thereby hangs a tale. Good faith, it is such another Nan! But, I detest, an honest maid as ever broke bread. We had an hour’s talk of that wart. I shall never laugh but in that maid’s company. But, indeed, she is given too much to allicholy and musing. But for you—well, go to.

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: Well, I shall see her today. Hold, there’s money for thee. Let me have thy voice in my behalf. If thou seest her before me, commend me.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Will I? I’ faith, that we will! And I will tell your worship more of the wart the next time we have confidence, and of other wooers.

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: Well, farewell, I am in great haste now.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Farewell to your worship.

div.p: Truly, an honest gentleman—but Anne loves him not, for I know Anne’s mind as well as another does. Out upon ’t, what have I forgot?

div.head: ACT II
SCENE I. Before Page’s house
div.stage: Enter Mistress Page reading a letter.

lg.l: What, have I scaped love-letters in the holiday-time of my beauty, and am I now a subject for them? Let me see.

Reads. Ask me no reason why I love you, for though Love use Reason for his precisian, he admits him not for his counsellor. You are not young, no more am I. Go to, then, there’s sympathy. You are merry, so am I. Ha, ha, then there’s more sympathy. You love sack, and so do I. Would you desire better sympathy? Let it suffice thee, Mistress Page, at the least, if the love of soldier can suffice, that I love thee. I will not say, pity me—’tis not a soldier-like phrase—but I say love me. By me,
Thine own true knight,
By day or night,
Or any kind of light,
With all his might,
For thee to fight,
John Falstaff.

What a Herod of Jewry is this! O wicked, wicked world! One that is well-nigh worn to pieces with age, to show himself a young gallant! What an unweighed behaviour hath this Flemish drunkard picked—with the devil’s name!—out of my conversation, that he dares in this manner assay me? Why, he hath not been thrice in my company! What should I say to him? I was then frugal of my mirth. Heaven forgive me! Why, I’ll exhibit a bill in the parliament for the putting down of men. How shall I be revenged on him? For revenged I will be, as sure as his guts are made of puddings.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Mistress Page! Trust me, I was going to your house.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: And, trust me, I was coming to you. You look very ill.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Nay, I’ll ne’er believe that. I have to show to the contrary.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Faith, but you do, in my mind.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Well, I do, then. Yet I say I could show you to the contrary. O, Mistress Page, give me some counsel.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: What’s the matter, woman?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: O woman, if it were not for one trifling respect, I could come to such honour!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Hang the trifle, woman; take the honour. What is it? Dispense with trifles. What is it?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: If I would but go to hell for an eternal moment or so, I could be knighted.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: What? Thou liest! Sir Alice Ford! These knights will hack, and so thou shouldst not alter the article of thy gentry.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: We burn daylight. Here, read, read. Perceive how I might be knighted. I shall think the worse of fat men as long as I have an eye to make difference of men’s liking. And yet he would not swear; praised women’s modesty; and gave such orderly and well-behaved reproof to all uncomeliness that I would have sworn his disposition would have gone to the truth of his words. But they do no more adhere and keep place together than the Hundredth Psalm to the tune of “Greensleeves.” What tempest, I trow, threw this whale, with so many tuns of oil in his belly, ashore at Windsor? How shall I be revenged on him? I think the best way were to entertain him with hope, till the wicked fire of lust have melted him in his own grease. Did you ever hear the like?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Letter for letter, but that the name of Page and Ford differs! To thy great comfort in this mystery of ill opinions, here’s the twin brother of thy letter. But let thine inherit first, for I protest mine never shall. I warrant he hath a thousand of these letters, writ with blank space for different names—sure, more, and these are of the second edition. He will print them, out of doubt; for he cares not what he puts into the press, when he would put us two. I had rather be a giantess and lie under Mount Pelion. Well, I will find you twenty lascivious turtles ere one chaste man.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Why, this is the very same—the very hand, the very words. What doth he think of us?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Nay, I know not. It makes me almost ready to wrangle with mine own honesty. I’ll entertain myself like one that I am not acquainted withal; for, sure, unless he know some strain in me that I know not myself, he would never have boarded me in this fury.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: “Boarding” call you it? I’ll be sure to keep him above deck.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: So will I. If he come under my hatches, I’ll never to sea again. Let’s be revenged on him. Let’s appoint him a meeting, give him a show of comfort in his suit, and lead him on with a fine-baited delay, till he hath pawned his horses to mine host of the Garter.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Nay, I will consent to act any villainy against him that may not sully the chariness of our honesty. O, that my husband saw this letter! It would give eternal food to his jealousy.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Why, look where he comes; and my good man too. He’s as far from jealousy as I am from giving him cause, and that, I hope, is an unmeasurable distance.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: You are the happier woman.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Let’s consult together against this greasy knight. Come hither.

div.stage: Enter Ford with Pistol, and Page with Nym.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Well, I hope it be not so.

lg.l: Hope is a curtal dog in some affairs.
Sir John affects thy wife.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Why, sir, my wife is not young.

lg.l: He woos both high and low, both rich and poor,
Both young and old, one with another, Ford.
He loves the gallimaufry. Ford, perpend.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Love my wife?

lg.l: With liver burning hot.
Prevent, or go thou like Sir Actaeon he,
With Ringwood at thy heels.
O, odious is the name!

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: What name, sir?

lg.l: The horn, I say. Farewell.
Take heed, have open eye, for thieves do foot by night.
Take heed, ere summer comes, or cuckoo birds do sing.—
Away, Sir Corporal Nym.—Believe it, Page, he speaks sense.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Aside. I will be patient. I will find out this.

sp.speaker: NYM
sp.p: To Page. And this is true, I like not the humour of lying. He hath wronged me in some humours. I should have borne the humoured letter to her; but I have a sword, and it shall bite upon my necessity. He loves your wife; there’s the short and the long. My name is Corporal Nym. I speak, and I avouch ’tis true. My name is Nym, and Falstaff loves your wife. Adieu. I love not the humour of bread and cheese. Adieu.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Aside. “The humour of it,” quoth ’a! Here’s a fellow frights English out of his wits.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Aside. I will seek out Falstaff.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Aside. I never heard such a drawling, affecting rogue.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Aside. If I do find it—well.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Aside. I will not believe such a Cataian, though the priest o’ the town commended him for a true man.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Aside. ’Twas a good sensible fellow—well.

div.stage: Mistress Page and Mistress Ford come forward.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: How now, Meg?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Whither go you, George? Hark you.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: How now, sweet Frank, why art thou melancholy?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I melancholy? I am not melancholy. Get you home, go.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Faith, thou hast some crotchets in thy head now.—Will you go, Mistress Page?

lg.l: Have with you. You’ll come to dinner, George?
Aside to Mistress Ford. Look who comes yonder. She shall be our messenger to this paltry knight.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Aside to Mistress Page. Trust me, I thought on her. She’ll fit it.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: You are come to see my daughter Anne?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Ay, forsooth. And, I pray, how does good Mistress Anne?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Go in with us and see. We’d have an hour’s talk with you.

div.stage: Exeunt Mistress Page, Mistress Ford and Mistress Quickly.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: How now, Master Ford?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: You heard what this knave told me, did you not?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Yes, and you heard what the other told me?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Do you think there is truth in them?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Hang ’em, slaves! I do not think the knight would offer it, but these that accuse him in his intent towards our wives are a yoke of his discarded men, very rogues, now they be out of service.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Were they his men?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Marry, were they.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I like it never the better for that. Does he lie at the Garter?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Ay, marry, does he. If he should intend this voyage toward my wife, I would turn her loose to him; and what he gets more of her than sharp words, let it lie on my head.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I do not misdoubt my wife, but I would be loath to turn them together. A man may be too confident. I would have nothing lie on my head. I cannot be thus satisfied.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Look where my ranting host of the Garter comes. There is either liquor in his pate or money in his purse when he looks so merrily.—How now, mine host?

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: How now, bully rook? Thou’rt a gentleman.—Cavaliero Justice, I say!

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: I follow, mine host, I follow.—Good even and twenty, good Master Page. Master Page, will you go with us? We have sport in hand.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Tell him, Cavaliero Justice; tell him, bully rook.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Sir, there is a fray to be fought between Sir Hugh the Welsh priest and Caius the French doctor.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Good mine host o’ the Garter, a word with you.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: What say’st thou, my bully rook?

div.stage: Ford and the Host talk apart.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: To Page. Will you go with us to behold it? My merry host hath had the measuring of their weapons, and, I think, hath appointed them contrary places; for, believe me, I hear the parson is no jester. Hark, I will tell you what our sport shall be.

div.stage: Shallow and Page talk apart. Ford and the Host come forward.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Hast thou no suit against my knight, my guest cavaliero?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: None, I protest. But I’ll give you a pottle of burnt sack to give me recourse to him, and tell him my name is Brook, only for a jest.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: My hand, bully. Thou shalt have egress and regress—said I well?—and thy name shall be Brook. It is a merry knight. Will you go, myn-heers?

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Have with you, mine host.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: I have heard the Frenchman hath good skill in his rapier.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Tut, sir, I could have told you more. In these times you stand on distance—your passes, stoccadoes, and I know not what. ’Tis the heart, Master Page; ’tis here, ’tis here. I have seen the time, with my long sword I would have made you four tall fellows skip like rats.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Here, boys, here, here! Shall we wag?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Have with you. I had rather hear them scold than fight.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Though Page be a secure fool, and stands so firmly on his wife’s frailty, yet I cannot put off my opinion so easily. She was in his company at Page’s house, and what they made there I know not. Well, I will look further into ’t, and I have a disguise to sound Falstaff. If I find her honest, I lose not my labour. If she be otherwise, ’tis labour well bestowed.

div.head: SCENE II. A room in the Garter Inn

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I will not lend thee a penny.

lg.l: Why then, the world’s mine oyster,
Which I with sword will open.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Not a penny. I have been content, sir, you should lay my countenance to pawn; I have grated upon my good friends for three reprieves for you and your coach-fellow Nym, or else you had looked through the grate like a gemini of baboons. I am damned in hell for swearing to gentlemen my friends you were good soldiers and tall fellows. And when Mistress Bridget lost the handle of her fan, I took ’t upon mine honour thou hadst it not.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: Didst not thou share? Hadst thou not fifteen pence?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Reason, you rogue, reason. Think’st thou I’ll endanger my soul gratis? At a word, hang no more about me, I am no gibbet for you. Go—a short knife and a throng—to your manor of Pickt-hatch, go. You’ll not bear a letter for me, you rogue? You stand upon your honour! Why, thou unconfinable baseness, it is as much as I can do to keep the terms of my honour precise. Ay, ay, I myself sometimes, leaving the fear of God on the left hand, and hiding mine honour in my necessity, am fain to shuffle, to hedge, and to lurch; and yet you, rogue, will ensconce your rags, your cat-a-mountain looks, your red-lattice phrases, and your bold beating oaths, under the shelter of your honour! You will not do it! You!

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: I do relent. What wouldst thou more of man?

sp.speaker: ROBIN
sp.p: Sir, here’s a woman would speak with you.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Let her approach.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Give your worship good morrow.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Good morrow, goodwife.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Not so, an’t please your worship.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Good maid, then.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: I’ll be sworn, as my mother was, the first hour I was born.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I do believe the swearer. What with me?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Shall I vouchsafe your worship a word or two?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Two thousand, fair woman; and I’ll vouchsafe thee the hearing.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: There is one Mistress Ford, sir—I pray, come a little nearer this ways. I myself dwell with Master Doctor Caius.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Well, on; Mistress Ford, you say—

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Your worship says very true. I pray your worship come a little nearer this ways.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I warrant thee, nobody hears. Mine own people, mine own people.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Are they so? God bless them, and make them His servants!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Well, Mistress Ford, what of her?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Why, sir, she’s a good creature. Lord, Lord, your worship’s a wanton! Well, heaven forgive you, and all of us, I pray!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Mistress Ford, come, Mistress Ford.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Marry, this is the short and the long of it: you have brought her into such a canaries as ’tis wonderful. The best courtier of them all, when the court lay at Windsor, could never have brought her to such a canary. Yet there has been knights, and lords, and gentlemen, with their coaches, I warrant you, coach after coach, letter after letter, gift after gift, smelling so sweetly, all musk, and so rushling, I warrant you, in silk and gold, and in such alligant terms, and in such wine and sugar of the best and the fairest, that would have won any woman’s heart; and I warrant you, they could never get an eye-wink of her. I had myself twenty angels given me this morning, but I defy all angels in any such sort, as they say, but in the way of honesty. And, I warrant you, they could never get her so much as sip on a cup with the proudest of them all. And yet there has been earls—nay, which is more, pensioners—but, I warrant you, all is one with her.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: But what says she to me? Be brief, my good she-Mercury.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Marry, she hath received your letter, for the which she thanks you a thousand times; and she gives you to notify that her husband will be absence from his house between ten and eleven.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Ten and eleven?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Ay, forsooth; and then you may come and see the picture, she says, that you wot of. Master Ford, her husband, will be from home. Alas, the sweet woman leads an ill life with him. He’s a very jealousy man; she leads a very frampold life with him, good heart.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Ten and eleven. Woman, commend me to her; I will not fail her.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Why, you say well. But I have another messenger to your worship. Mistress Page hath her hearty commendations to you too; and let me tell you in your ear, she’s as fartuous a civil modest wife, and one, I tell you, that will not miss you morning nor evening prayer, as any is in Windsor, whoe’er be the other; and she bade me tell your worship that her husband is seldom from home, but she hopes there will come a time. I never knew a woman so dote upon a man. Surely I think you have charms, la! Yes, in truth.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Not I, I assure thee. Setting the attraction of my good parts aside, I have no other charms.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Blessing on your heart for ’t!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: But, I pray thee, tell me this: has Ford’s wife and Page’s wife acquainted each other how they love me?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: That were a jest indeed! They have not so little grace, I hope. That were a trick indeed! But Mistress Page would desire you to send her your little page, of all loves. Her husband has a marvellous infection to the little page; and, truly, Master Page is an honest man. Never a wife in Windsor leads a better life than she does. Do what she will, say what she will, take all, pay all, go to bed when she list, rise when she list, all is as she will, and truly she deserves it, for if there be a kind woman in Windsor, she is one. You must send her your page, no remedy.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Why, I will.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Nay, but do so then, and, look you, he may come and go between you both; and in any case have a nay-word, that you may know one another’s mind, and the boy never need to understand anything; for ’tis not good that children should know any wickedness. Old folks, you know, have discretion, as they say, and know the world.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Fare thee well, commend me to them both. There’s my purse; I am yet thy debtor. Boy, go along with this woman.—This news distracts me.

lg.l: This punk is one of Cupid’s carriers;
Clap on more sails, pursue; up with your fights;
Give fire! She is my prize, or ocean whelm them all!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Sayst thou so, old Jack? Go thy ways, I’ll make more of thy old body than I have done. Will they yet look after thee? Wilt thou, after the expense of so much money, be now a gainer? Good body, I thank thee. Let them say ’tis grossly done; so it be fairly done, no matter.

div.stage: Enter Bardolph with a cup of sack.

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Sir John, there’s one Master Brook below would fain speak with you and be acquainted with you, and hath sent your worship a morning’s draught of sack.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Brook is his name?

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Ay, sir.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Call him in.

div.p: Such Brooks are welcome to me, that o’erflow such liquor. Ah, ha, Mistress Ford and Mistress Page, have I encompassed you? Go to, via!
div.stage: Enter Bardolph with Ford disguised as Brook.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: God bless you, sir.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: And you, sir. Would you speak with me?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I make bold to press with so little preparation upon you.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: You’re welcome. What’s your will?—Give us leave, drawer.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Sir, I am a gentleman that have spent much. My name is Brook.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Good Master Brook, I desire more acquaintance of you.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Good Sir John, I sue for yours; not to charge you, for I must let you understand I think myself in better plight for a lender than you are, the which hath something emboldened me to this unseasoned intrusion; for they say, if money go before, all ways do lie open.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Money is a good soldier, sir, and will on.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Troth, and I have a bag of money here troubles me. If you will help to bear it, Sir John, take all, or half, for easing me of the carriage.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Sir, I know not how I may deserve to be your porter.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I will tell you, sir, if you will give me the hearing.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Speak, good Master Brook. I shall be glad to be your servant.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Sir, I hear you are a scholar—I will be brief with you—and you have been a man long known to me, though I had never so good means as desire to make myself acquainted with you. I shall discover a thing to you, wherein I must very much lay open mine own imperfection. But, good Sir John, as you have one eye upon my follies, as you hear them unfolded, turn another into the register of your own, that I may pass with a reproof the easier, sith you yourself know how easy it is to be such an offender.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Very well, sir, proceed.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: There is a gentlewoman in this town, her husband’s name is Ford.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Well, sir.

lg.l: I have long loved her, and, I protest to you, bestowed much on her, followed her with a doting observance, engrossed opportunities to meet her, fee’d every slight occasion that could but niggardly give me sight of her, not only bought many presents to give her, but have given largely to many to know what she would have given. Briefly, I have pursued her as love hath pursued me, which hath been on the wing of all occasions. But whatsoever I have merited, either in my mind or in my means, meed, I am sure, I have received none, unless experience be a jewel. That I have purchased at an infinite rate, and that hath taught me to say this:
Love like a shadow flies when substance love pursues,
Pursuing that that flies, and flying what pursues.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Have you received no promise of satisfaction at her hands?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Never.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Have you importuned her to such a purpose?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Never.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Of what quality was your love, then?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Like a fair house built on another man’s ground, so that I have lost my edifice by mistaking the place where I erected it.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: To what purpose have you unfolded this to me?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: When I have told you that, I have told you all. Some say that though she appear honest to me, yet in other places she enlargeth her mirth so far that there is shrewd construction made of her. Now, Sir John, here is the heart of my purpose: you are a gentleman of excellent breeding, admirable discourse, of great admittance, authentic in your place and person, generally allowed for your many warlike, courtlike, and learned preparations.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: O, sir!

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Believe it, for you know it. There is money. Spend it, spend it; spend more; spend all I have; only give me so much of your time in exchange of it as to lay an amiable siege to the honesty of this Ford’s wife. Use your art of wooing, win her to consent to you. If any man may, you may as soon as any.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Would it apply well to the vehemency of your affection that I should win what you would enjoy? Methinks you prescribe to yourself very preposterously.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: O, understand my drift. She dwells so securely on the excellency of her honour that the folly of my soul dares not present itself; she is too bright to be looked against. Now, could I come to her with any detection in my hand, my desires had instance and argument to commend themselves. I could drive her then from the ward of her purity, her reputation, her marriage vow, and a thousand other her defences, which now are too too strongly embattled against me. What say you to’t, Sir John?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Master Brook, I will first make bold with your money; next, give me your hand; and last, as I am a gentleman, you shall, if you will, enjoy Ford’s wife.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: O good sir!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I say you shall.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Want no money, Sir John; you shall want none.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Want no Mistress Ford, Master Brook; you shall want none. I shall be with her, I may tell you, by her own appointment; even as you came in to me, her assistant or go-between parted from me. I say I shall be with her between ten and eleven, for at that time the jealous rascally knave her husband will be forth. Come you to me at night. You shall know how I speed.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I am blessed in your acquaintance. Do you know Ford, sir?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Hang him, poor cuckoldly knave! I know him not. Yet I wrong him to call him poor. They say the jealous wittolly knave hath masses of money, for the which his wife seems to me well-favoured. I will use her as the key of the cuckoldly rogue’s coffer, and there’s my harvest-home.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I would you knew Ford, sir, that you might avoid him if you saw him.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Hang him, mechanical salt-butter rogue! I will stare him out of his wits, I will awe him with my cudgel; it shall hang like a meteor o’er the cuckold’s horns. Master Brook, thou shalt know I will predominate over the peasant, and thou shalt lie with his wife. Come to me soon at night. Ford’s a knave, and I will aggravate his style. Thou, Master Brook, shalt know him for knave and cuckold. Come to me soon at night.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: What a damned epicurean rascal is this! My heart is ready to crack with impatience. Who says this is improvident jealousy? My wife hath sent to him, the hour is fixed, the match is made. Would any man have thought this? See the hell of having a false woman: my bed shall be abused, my coffers ransacked, my reputation gnawn at; and I shall not only receive this villanous wrong, but stand under the adoption of abominable terms, and by him that does me this wrong. Terms, names! Amaimon sounds well; Lucifer, well; Barbason, well; yet they are devils’ additions, the names of fiends. But cuckold? Wittol? Cuckold? The devil himself hath not such a name. Page is an ass, a secure ass; he will trust his wife, he will not be jealous. I will rather trust a Fleming with my butter, Parson Hugh the Welshman with my cheese, an Irishman with my aqua-vitae bottle, or a thief to walk my ambling gelding, than my wife with herself. Then she plots, then she ruminates, then she devises; and what they think in their hearts they may effect, they will break their hearts but they will effect. God be praised for my jealousy! Eleven o’clock the hour. I will prevent this, detect my wife, be revenged on Falstaff, and laugh at Page. I will about it. Better three hours too soon than a minute too late. Fie, fie, fie! Cuckold, cuckold, cuckold!

div.head: SCENE III. A field near Windsor

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Jack Rugby!

sp.speaker: RUGBY
sp.p: Sir?

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Vat is de clock, Jack?

sp.speaker: RUGBY
sp.p: ’Tis past the hour, sir, that Sir Hugh promised to meet.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, he has save his soul, dat he is no come. He has pray his Pible well dat he is no come. By gar, Jack Rugby, he is dead already, if he be come.

sp.speaker: RUGBY
sp.p: He is wise, sir; he knew your worship would kill him if he came.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, de herring is no dead so as I vill kill him. Take your rapier, Jack; I vill tell you how I vill kill him.

sp.speaker: RUGBY
sp.p: Alas, sir, I cannot fence.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Villainy, take your rapier.

sp.speaker: RUGBY
sp.p: Forbear; here’s company.

div.stage: Enter Page, Shallow, Slender and Host.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: God bless thee, bully doctor!

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: God save you, Master Doctor Caius!

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Now, good Master Doctor!

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Give you good morrow, sir.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Vat be all you, one, two, tree, four, come for?

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: To see thee fight, to see thee foin, to see thee traverse; to see thee here, to see thee there; to see thee pass thy punto, thy stock, thy reverse, thy distance, thy montant. Is he dead, my Ethiopian? Is he dead, my Francisco? Ha, bully? What says my Aesculapius, my Galen, my heart of elder, ha? Is he dead, bully stale? Is he dead?

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, he is de coward Jack-priest of de vorld. He is not show his face.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Thou art a Castalion King Urinal Hector of Greece, my boy!

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: I pray you, bear witness that me have stay six or seven, two, tree hours for him, and he is no come.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: He is the wiser man, Master doctor. He is a curer of souls, and you a curer of bodies. If you should fight, you go against the hair of your professions. Is it not true, Master Page?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Master Shallow, you have yourself been a great fighter, though now a man of peace.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Bodykins, Master Page, though I now be old, and of the peace, if I see a sword out, my finger itches to make one. Though we are justices and doctors and churchmen, Master Page, we have some salt of our youth in us. We are the sons of women, Master Page.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: ’Tis true, Master Shallow.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: It will be found so, Master Page.—Master Doctor Caius, I come to fetch you home. I am sworn of the peace. You have showed yourself a wise physician, and Sir Hugh hath shown himself a wise and patient churchman. You must go with me, Master Doctor.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Pardon, guest justice.—A word, Monsieur Mockwater.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Mockvater? Vat is dat?

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Mockwater, in our English tongue, is valour, bully.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, then I have as much mockvater as de Englishman. Scurvy jack-dog priest! By gar, me vill cut his ears.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: He will clapper-claw thee tightly, bully.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Clapper-de-claw? Vat is dat?

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: That is, he will make thee amends.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, me do look he shall clapper-de-claw me, for, by gar, me vill have it.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: And I will provoke him to’t, or let him wag.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Me tank you for dat.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: And, moreover, bully—but first, Master guest, and Master Page, and eke Cavaliero Slender, go you through the town to Frogmore.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Aside to Host. Sir Hugh is there, is he?

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Aside to Page. He is there. See what humour he is in; and I will bring the doctor about by the fields. Will it do well?

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Aside to Host. We will do it.

div.p: PAGE, SHALLOW and SLENDER Adieu, good Master Doctor.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, me vill kill de priest, for he speak for a jackanape to Anne Page.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Let him die. Sheathe thy impatience; throw cold water on thy choler. Go about the fields with me through Frogmore. I will bring thee where Mistress Anne Page is, at a farm-house a-feasting, and thou shalt woo her. Cried game! Said I well?

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, me tank you for dat. By gar, I love you; and I shall procure-a you de good guest: de earl, de knight, de lords, de gentlemen, my patients.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: For the which I will be thy adversary toward Anne Page. Said I well?

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, ’tis good; vell said.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Let us wag, then.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Come at my heels, Jack Rugby.

div.head: ACT III
SCENE I. A field near Frogmore
div.stage: Enter Sir Hugh Evans and Simple.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: I pray you now, good Master Slender’s servingman, and friend Simple by your name, which way have you looked for Master Caius, that calls himself doctor of physic?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Marry, sir, the Petty-ward, the Park-ward, every way; old Windsor way, and every way but the town way.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: I most fehemently desire you, you will also look that way.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: I will, Sir.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Pless my soul, how full of cholers I am, and trempling of mind! I shall be glad if he have deceived me. How melancholies I am! I will knog his urinals about his knave’s costard when I have good opportunities for the ’ork. Pless my soul!

div.p: To shallow rivers, to whose falls Melodious birds sings madrigals. There will we make our peds of roses And a thousand fragrant posies. To shallow— Mercy on me, I have a great dispositions to cry.

p.emph: Melodious birds sing madrigals— Whenas I sat in Pabylon— And a thousand vagram posies. To shallow rivers, to whose falls Melodious birds sing madrigals.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Yonder he is, coming this way, Sir Hugh.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: He’s welcome.

div.p: Sings. To shallow rivers, to whose falls— Heaven prosper the right! What weapons is he?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: No weapons, sir. There comes my master, Master Shallow, and another gentleman, from Frogmore, over the stile, this way.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Pray you, give me my gown—or else keep it in your arms.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: How now, Master Parson? Good morrow, good Sir Hugh. Keep a gamester from the dice, and a good student from his book, and it is wonderful.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Aside. Ah, sweet Anne Page!

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: God save you, good Sir Hugh!

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: God pless you from his mercy sake, all of you!

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: What, the sword and the word? Do you study them both, Master Parson?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: And youthful still—in your doublet and hose, this raw rheumatic day?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: There is reasons and causes for it.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: We are come to you to do a good office, Master Parson.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Fery well; what is it?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Yonder is a most reverend gentleman who, belike having received wrong by some person, is at most odds with his own gravity and patience that ever you saw.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: I have lived fourscore years and upward; I never heard a man of his place, gravity, and learning, so wide of his own respect.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: What is he?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: I think you know him: Master Doctor Caius, the renowned French physician.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Got’s will and His passion of my heart! I had as lief you would tell me of a mess of porridge.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Why?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: He has no more knowledge in Hibbocrates and Galen, and he is a knave besides, a cowardly knave as you would desires to be acquainted withal.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: I warrant you, he’s the man should fight with him.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Aside. O, sweet Anne Page!

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: It appears so by his weapons. Keep them asunder. Here comes Doctor Caius.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Nay, good Master Parson, keep in your weapon.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: So do you, good Master Doctor.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Disarm them, and let them question. Let them keep their limbs whole and hack our English.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: I pray you, let-a me speak a word with your ear. Verefore will you not meet-a me?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Aside to Caius. Pray you, use your patience. In good time.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, you are de coward, de Jack dog, John ape.

lg.l: Aside to Caius. Pray you, let us not be laughing stocks to other men’s humours. I desire you in friendship, and I will one way or other make you amends.
Aloud. By Jeshu, I will knog your urinal about your knave’s cogscomb.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Diable! Jack Rugby, mine Host de Jarteer, have I not stay for him to kill him? Have I not, at de place I did appoint?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: As I am a Christians soul, now look you, this is the place appointed. I’ll be judgment by mine host of the Garter.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Peace, I say, Gallia and Gaul, French and Welsh, soul-curer and body-curer!

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Ay, dat is very good; excellent.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Peace, I say! Hear mine host of the Garter. Am I politic? Am I subtle? Am I a Machiavel? Shall I lose my doctor? No, he gives me the potions and the motions. Shall I lose my parson, my priest, my Sir Hugh? No, he gives me the proverbs and the no-verbs. To Caius. Give me thy hand, terrestrial; so. To Evans. Give me thy hand, celestial; so. Boys of art, I have deceived you both. I have directed you to wrong places. Your hearts are mighty, your skins are whole, and let burnt sack be the issue. Come, lay their swords to pawn. Follow me, lads of peace, follow, follow, follow.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Afore God, a mad host! Follow, gentlemen, follow.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Aside. O, sweet Anne Page!

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Ha, do I perceive dat? Have you make-a de sot of us, ha, ha?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: This is well, he has made us his vlouting-stog. I desire you that we may be friends, and let us knog our prains together to be revenge on this same scall, scurvy, cogging companion, the host of the Garter.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, with all my heart. He promise to bring me where is Anne Page; by gar, he deceive me too.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Well, I will smite his noddles. Pray you follow.

div.head: SCENE II. A street in Windsor

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Nay, keep your way, little gallant. You were wont to be a follower, but now you are a leader. Whether had you rather, lead mine eyes, or eye your master’s heels?

sp.speaker: ROBIN
sp.p: I had rather, forsooth, go before you like a man than follow him like a dwarf.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: O, you are a flattering boy! Now I see you’ll be a courtier.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Well met, Mistress Page. Whither go you?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Truly, sir, to see your wife. Is she at home?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Ay, and as idle as she may hang together, for want of company. I think if your husbands were dead you two would marry.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Be sure of that—two other husbands.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Where had you this pretty weathercock?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: I cannot tell what the dickens his name is my husband had him of. What do you call your knight’s name, sirrah?

sp.speaker: ROBIN
sp.p: Sir John Falstaff.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Sir John Falstaff!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: He, he; I can never hit on’s name. There is such a league between my good man and he! Is your wife at home indeed?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Indeed she is.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: By your leave, sir, I am sick till I see her.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Has Page any brains? Hath he any eyes? Hath he any thinking? Sure, they sleep; he hath no use of them. Why, this boy will carry a letter twenty mile as easy as a cannon will shoot point-blank twelve score. He pieces out his wife’s inclination, he gives her folly motion and advantage. And now she’s going to my wife, and Falstaff’s boy with her. A man may hear this shower sing in the wind. And Falstaff’s boy with her! Good plots they are laid, and our revolted wives share damnation together. Well, I will take him, then torture my wife, pluck the borrowed veil of modesty from the so-seeming Mistress Page, divulge Page himself for a secure and wilful Actaeon, and to these violent proceedings all my neighbours shall cry aim. Clock strikes. The clock gives me my cue, and my assurance bids me search. There I shall find Falstaff. I shall be rather praised for this than mocked, for it is as positive as the earth is firm that Falstaff is there. I will go.

div.stage: Enter Page, Shallow, Slender, Host, Sir Hugh Evans, Caius and Rugby.
div.p: SHALLOW, PAGE, etc. Well met, Master Ford.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Trust me, a good knot. I have good cheer at home, and I pray you all go with me.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: I must excuse myself, Master Ford.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: And so must I, sir; we have appointed to dine with Mistress Anne, and I would not break with her for more money than I’ll speak of.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: We have lingered about a match between Anne Page and my cousin Slender, and this day we shall have our answer.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I hope I have your good will, father Page.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: You have, Master Slender, I stand wholly for you.—But my wife, Master doctor, is for you altogether.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Ay, be-gar; and de maid is love-a me! My nursh-a Quickly tell me so mush.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: What say you to young Master Fenton? He capers, he dances, he has eyes of youth, he writes verses, he speaks holiday, he smells April and May. He will carry ’t, he will carry ’t. ’Tis in his buttons he will carry ’t.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Not by my consent, I promise you. The gentleman is of no having. He kept company with the wild Prince and Poins. He is of too high a region, he knows too much. No, he shall not knit a knot in his fortunes with the finger of my substance. If he take her, let him take her simply. The wealth I have waits on my consent, and my consent goes not that way.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I beseech you, heartily, some of you go home with me to dinner. Besides your cheer, you shall have sport: I will show you a monster. Master Doctor, you shall go; so shall you, Master Page, and you, Sir Hugh.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Well, fare you well. We shall have the freer wooing at Master Page’s.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Go home, John Rugby; I come anon.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Farewell, my hearts. I will to my honest knight Falstaff, and drink canary with him.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Aside. I think I shall drink in pipe-wine first with him; I’ll make him dance.—Will you go, gentles?

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: Have with you to see this monster.

div.head: SCENE III. A room in Ford’s house
div.stage: Enter Mistress Ford and Mistress Page.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: What, John! What, Robert!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Quickly, quickly! Is the buck-basket—

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I warrant.—What, Robin, I say!

div.stage: Enter John and Robert with a great buck-basket.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Come, come, come.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Here, set it down.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Give your men the charge; we must be brief.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Marry, as I told you before, John and Robert, be ready here hard by in the brew-house; and when I suddenly call you, come forth, and, without any pause or staggering, take this basket on your shoulders. That done, trudge with it in all haste, and carry it among the whitsters in Datchet Mead, and there empty it in the muddy ditch close by the Thames side.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: You will do it?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I ha’ told them over and over, they lack no direction.—Be gone, and come when you are called.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Here comes little Robin.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: How now, my eyas-musket, what news with you?

sp.speaker: ROBIN
sp.p: My Master, Sir John, is come in at your back door, Mistress Ford, and requests your company.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: You little Jack-a-Lent, have you been true to us?

sp.speaker: ROBIN
sp.p: Ay, I’ll be sworn. My master knows not of your being here, and hath threatened to put me into everlasting liberty if I tell you of it; for he swears he’ll turn me away.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Thou’rt a good boy, this secrecy of thine shall be a tailor to thee, and shall make thee a new doublet and hose. I’ll go hide me.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Do so.—Go tell thy master I am alone.

div.p: Mistress Page, remember you your cue.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: I warrant thee. If I do not act it, hiss me.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Go to, then. We’ll use this unwholesome humidity, this gross watery pumpion; we’ll teach him to know turtles from jays.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: “Have I caught thee, my heavenly jewel?” Why, now let me die, for I have lived long enough. This is the period of my ambition. O this blessed hour!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: O, sweet Sir John!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Mistress Ford, I cannot cog, I cannot prate, Mistress Ford. Now shall I sin in my wish: I would thy husband were dead. I’ll speak it before the best lord: I would make thee my lady.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I your lady, Sir John? Alas, I should be a pitiful lady.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Let the court of France show me such another. I see how thine eye would emulate the diamond. Thou hast the right arched beauty of the brow that becomes the ship-tire, the tire-valiant, or any tire of Venetian admittance.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: A plain kerchief, Sir John. My brows become nothing else, nor that well neither.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: By the Lord, thou art a traitor to say so. Thou wouldst make an absolute courtier, and the firm fixture of thy foot would give an excellent motion to thy gait in a semi-circled farthingale. I see what thou wert, if Fortune thy foe were not, Nature thy friend. Come, thou canst not hide it.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Believe me, there’s no such thing in me.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: What made me love thee? Let that persuade thee there’s something extraordinary in thee. Come, I cannot cog and say thou art this and that, like a many of these lisping hawthorn buds that come like women in men’s apparel, and smell like Bucklersbury in simple-time. I cannot. But I love thee, none but thee; and thou deservest it.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Do not betray me, sir; I fear you love Mistress Page.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Thou mightst as well say I love to walk by the Counter gate, which is as hateful to me as the reek of a lime-kiln.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Well, heaven knows how I love you, and you shall one day find it.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Keep in that mind, I’ll deserve it.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Nay, I must tell you, so you do; or else I could not be in that mind.

sp.speaker: ROBIN
sp.p: Mistress Ford, Mistress Ford, here’s Mistress Page at the door, sweating and blowing and looking wildly, and would needs speak with you presently.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: She shall not see me; I will ensconce me behind the arras.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Pray you, do so; she’s a very tattling woman.

div.stage: Falstaff hides himself behind the arras.
div.p: What’s the matter? How now?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: O Mistress Ford, what have you done? You’re shamed, you’re overthrown, you’re undone for ever!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: What’s the matter, good Mistress Page?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: O well-a-day, Mistress Ford, having an honest man to your husband, to give him such cause of suspicion!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: What cause of suspicion?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: What cause of suspicion? Out upon you! How am I mistook in you!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Why, alas, what’s the matter?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Your husband’s coming hither, woman, with all the officers in Windsor, to search for a gentleman that he says is here now in the house, by your consent, to take an ill advantage of his absence. You are undone.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: ’Tis not so, I hope.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Pray heaven it be not so, that you have such a man here! But ’tis most certain your husband’s coming, with half Windsor at his heels, to search for such a one. I come before to tell you. If you know yourself clear, why, I am glad of it; but if you have a friend here, convey, convey him out. Be not amazed, call all your senses to you; defend your reputation, or bid farewell to your good life for ever.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: What shall I do? There is a gentleman, my dear friend; and I fear not mine own shame as much as his peril. I had rather than a thousand pound he were out of the house.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: For shame! Never stand “you had rather” and “you had rather”. Your husband’s here at hand. Bethink you of some conveyance. In the house you cannot hide him. O, how have you deceived me! Look, here is a basket. If he be of any reasonable stature, he may creep in here; and throw foul linen upon him, as if it were going to bucking. Or—it is whiting-time—send him by your two men to Datchet Mead.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: He’s too big to go in there. What shall I do?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Comes out of hiding. Let me see ’t, let me see ’t! O, let me see ’t! I’ll in, I’ll in. Follow your friend’s counsel. I’ll in.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: What, Sir John Falstaff? Are these your letters, knight?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I love thee, and none but thee. Help me away. Let me creep in here. I’ll never—

div.stage: He goes into the basket; they cover him with dirty clothes.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Help to cover your master, boy.—Call your men, Mistress Ford.—You dissembling knight!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: What, John! Robert! John!

div.p: Go, take up these clothes here, quickly. Where’s the cowl-staff? Look how you drumble! Carry them to the laundress in Datchet Mead; quickly, come.
div.stage: Enter Ford, Page, Caius and Sir Hugh Evans.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Pray you come near. If I suspect without cause, why then make sport at me, then let me be your jest; I deserve it.—How now? Whither bear you this?

div.p: JOHN and ROBERT. To the laundress, forsooth.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Why, what have you to do whither they bear it? You were best meddle with buck-washing!

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Buck? I would I could wash myself of the buck! Buck, buck, buck! Ay, buck! I warrant you, buck, and of the season too, it shall appear.

div.stage: Exeunt John and Robert with the basket.
