div.p: Gentlemen, I have dreamed tonight; I’ll tell you my dream. Here, here, here be my keys. Ascend my chambers, search, seek, find out. I’ll warrant we’ll unkennel the fox. Let me stop this way first. Locks the door. So, now uncape.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Good Master Ford, be contented: you wrong yourself too much.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: True, Master Page.—Up, gentlemen, you shall see sport anon. Follow me, gentlemen.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: This is fery fantastical humours and jealousies.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, ’tis no the fashion of France; it is not jealous in France.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Nay, follow him, gentlemen; see the issue of his search.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Is there not a double excellency in this?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I know not which pleases me better, that my husband is deceived, or Sir John.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: What a taking was he in when your husband asked who was in the basket!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I am half afraid he will have need of washing, so throwing him into the water will do him a benefit.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Hang him, dishonest rascal! I would all of the same strain were in the same distress.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I think my husband hath some special suspicion of Falstaff’s being here, for I never saw him so gross in his jealousy till now.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: I will lay a plot to try that, and we will yet have more tricks with Falstaff. His dissolute disease will scarce obey this medicine.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Shall we send that foolish carrion Mistress Quickly to him, and excuse his throwing into the water, and give him another hope, to betray him to another punishment?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: We will do it. Let him be sent for tomorrow eight o’clock to have amends.

div.stage: Enter Ford, Page, Caius and Sir Hugh Evans.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I cannot find him. Maybe the knave bragged of that he could not compass.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Aside to Mistress Ford. Heard you that?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: You use me well, Master Ford, do you?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Ay, I do so.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Heaven make you better than your thoughts!

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Amen!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: You do yourself mighty wrong, Master Ford.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Ay, ay; I must bear it.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: If there be anypody in the house, and in the chambers, and in the coffers, and in the presses, heaven forgive my sins at the day of judgment!

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Be gar, nor I too; there is nobodies.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Fie, fie, Master Ford, are you not ashamed? What spirit, what devil suggests this imagination? I would not ha’ your distemper in this kind for the wealth of Windsor Castle.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: ’Tis my fault, Master Page. I suffer for it.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: You suffer for a pad conscience. Your wife is as honest a ’omans as I will desires among five thousand, and five hundred too.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: By gar, I see ’tis an honest woman.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Well, I promised you a dinner. Come, come, walk in the park. I pray you pardon me; I will hereafter make known to you why I have done this. Come, wife, come, Mistress Page, I pray you pardon me. Pray heartily, pardon me.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Let’s go in, gentlemen; but, trust me, we’ll mock him. I do invite you tomorrow morning to my house to breakfast; after, we’ll a-birding together; I have a fine hawk for the bush. Shall it be so?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Anything.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: If there is one, I shall make two in the company.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: If there be one or two, I shall make-a the turd.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Pray you go, Master Page.

div.stage: Exeunt all but Evans and Caius.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: I pray you now, remembrance tomorrow on the lousy knave, mine host.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Dat is good, by gar, with all my heart.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: A lousy knave, to have his gibes and his mockeries!

div.head: SCENE IV. A room in Page’s house

lg.l: I see I cannot get thy father’s love;
Therefore no more turn me to him, sweet Nan.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: Alas, how then?

lg.l: Why, thou must be thyself.
He doth object I am too great of birth,
And that my state being galled with my expense,
I seek to heal it only by his wealth.
Besides these, other bars he lays before me:
My riots past, my wild societies—
And tells me ’tis a thing impossible
I should love thee but as a property.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: Maybe he tells you true.

lg.l: No, heaven so speed me in my time to come!
Albeit I will confess thy father’s wealth
Was the first motive that I wooed thee, Anne,
Yet, wooing thee, I found thee of more value
Than stamps in gold or sums in sealed bags.
And ’tis the very riches of thyself
That now I aim at.
Gentle Master Fenton,
Yet seek my father’s love, still seek it, sir.
If opportunity and humblest suit
Cannot attain it, why then—hark you hither.

div.stage: Enter Shallow, Slender and Mistress Quickly.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Break their talk, Mistress Quickly. My kinsman shall speak for himself.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I’ll make a shaft or a bolt on ’t. ’Slid, ’tis but venturing.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Be not dismayed.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: No, she shall not dismay me. I care not for that, but that I am afeard.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Hark ye, Master Slender would speak a word with you.

lg.l: I come to him.
Aside. This is my father’s choice.
O, what a world of vile ill-favoured faults
Looks handsome in three hundred pounds a year!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: And how does good Master Fenton? Pray you, a word with you.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: To Slender. She’s coming; to her, coz. O boy, thou hadst a father!

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I had a father, Mistress Anne; my uncle can tell you good jests of him.—Pray you, uncle, tell Mistress Anne the jest how my father stole two geese out of a pen, good uncle.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Mistress Anne, my cousin loves you.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, that I do, as well as I love any woman in Gloucestershire.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: He will maintain you like a gentlewoman.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, that I will, come cut and long-tail, under the degree of a squire.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: He will make you a hundred and fifty pounds jointure.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: Good Master Shallow, let him woo for himself.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Marry, I thank you for it, I thank you for that good comfort.—She calls you, coz; I’ll leave you.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: Now, Master Slender.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Now, good Mistress Anne.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: What is your will?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: My will? ’Od’s heartlings, that’s a pretty jest indeed! I ne’er made my will yet, I thank heaven. I am not such a sickly creature, I give heaven praise.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: I mean, Master Slender, what would you with me?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Truly, for mine own part I would little or nothing with you. Your father and my uncle hath made motions. If it be my luck, so; if not, happy man be his dole. They can tell you how things go better than I can. You may ask your father. Here he comes.

lg.l: Now, Master Slender.—Love him, daughter Anne.—
Why, how now? What does Master Fenton here?
You wrong me, sir, thus still to haunt my house.
I told you, sir, my daughter is disposed of.

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: Nay, Master Page, be not impatient.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Good Master Fenton, come not to my child.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: She is no match for you.

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: Sir, will you hear me?

lg.l: No, good Master Fenton.—
Come, Master Shallow; come, son Slender, in.—
Knowing my mind, you wrong me, Master Fenton.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Speak to Mistress Page.

lg.l: Good Mistress Page, for that I love your daughter
In such a righteous fashion as I do,
Perforce, against all checks, rebukes, and manners,
I must advance the colours of my love
And not retire. Let me have your good will.

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: Good mother, do not marry me to yond fool.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: I mean it not; I seek you a better husband.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: That’s my master, Master Doctor.

lg.l: Alas, I had rather be set quick i’ th’ earth,
And bowled to death with turnips.
Come, trouble not yourself, good Master Fenton,
I will not be your friend, nor enemy.
My daughter will I question how she loves you,
And as I find her, so am I affected.
Till then, farewell, sir. She must needs go in;
Her father will be angry.

sp.speaker: FENTON
sp.p: Farewell, gentle mistress. Farewell, Nan.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: This is my doing now. “Nay,” said I, “will you cast away your child on a fool, and a physician? Look on Master Fenton.” This is my doing.

lg.l: I thank thee; and I pray thee, once tonight
Give my sweet Nan this ring. There’s for thy pains.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Now Heaven send thee good fortune!

div.p: A kind heart he hath. A woman would run through fire and water for such a kind heart. But yet I would my master had Mistress Anne, or I would Master Slender had her; or, in sooth, I would Master Fenton had her. I will do what I can for them all three, for so I have promised and I’ll be as good as my word—but speciously for Master Fenton. Well, I must of another errand to Sir John Falstaff from my two mistresses. What a beast am I to slack it!

div.head: SCENE V. A room in the Garter Inn

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Bardolph, I say!

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Here, sir.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Go fetch me a quart of sack; put a toast in ’t.

div.p: Have I lived to be carried in a basket like a barrow of butcher’s offal, and to be thrown in the Thames? Well, if I be served such another trick, I’ll have my brains ta’en out and buttered, and give them to a dog for a New Year’s gift. ’Sblood, the rogues slighted me into the river with as little remorse as they would have drowned a blind bitch’s puppies, fifteen i’ the litter; and you may know by my size that I have a kind of alacrity in sinking; if the bottom were as deep as hell, I should down. I had been drowned, but that the shore was shelvy and shallow—a death that I abhor, for the water swells a man, and what a thing should I have been when I had been swelled! I should have been a mountain of mummy.

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Here’s Mistress Quickly, sir, to speak with you.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Come, let me pour in some sack to the Thames water, for my belly’s as cold as if I had swallowed snowballs for pills to cool the reins. Call her in.

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Come in, woman.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: By your leave, I cry you mercy. Give your worship good morrow.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Take away these chalices. Go, brew me a pottle of sack finely.

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: With eggs, sir?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Simple of itself. I’ll no pullet sperm in my brewage.

div.p: How now?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Marry, sir, I come to your worship from Mistress Ford.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Mistress Ford? I have had ford enough. I was thrown into the ford, I have my belly full of ford.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Alas the day, good heart, that was not her fault. She does so take on with her men; they mistook their erection.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: So did I mine, to build upon a foolish woman’s promise.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Well, she laments, sir, for it, that it would yearn your heart to see it. Her husband goes this morning a-birding; she desires you once more to come to her, between eight and nine. I must carry her word quickly. She’ll make you amends, I warrant you.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Well, I will visit her. Tell her so, and bid her think what a man is. Let her consider his frailty, and then judge of my merit.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: I will tell her.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Do so. Between nine and ten, sayst thou?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Eight and nine, sir.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Well, be gone. I will not miss her.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Peace be with you, sir.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I marvel I hear not of Master Brook; he sent me word to stay within. I like his money well. O, here he comes.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: God bless you, sir.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Now, Master Brook, you come to know what hath passed between me and Ford’s wife?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: That indeed, Sir John, is my business.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Master Brook, I will not lie to you. I was at her house the hour she appointed me.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: And how sped you, sir?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Very ill-favouredly, Master Brook.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: How so, sir? Did she change her determination?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: No. Master Brook, but the peaking cornuto her husband, Master Brook, dwelling in a continual ’larum of jealousy, comes me in the instant of our encounter, after we had embraced, kissed, protested, and, as it were, spoke the prologue of our comedy; and at his heels a rabble of his companions, thither provoked and instigated by his distemper, and, forsooth, to search his house for his wife’s love.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: What, while you were there?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: While I was there.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: And did he search for you, and could not find you?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: You shall hear. As good luck would have it, comes in one Mistress Page, gives intelligence of Ford’s approach; and, in her invention and Ford’s wife’s distraction, they conveyed me into a buck-basket.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: A buck-basket!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: By the Lord, a buck-basket! Rammed me in with foul shirts and smocks, socks, foul stockings, greasy napkins, that, Master Brook, there was the rankest compound of villainous smell that ever offended nostril.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: And how long lay you there?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Nay, you shall hear, Master Brook, what I have suffered to bring this woman to evil for your good. Being thus crammed in the basket, a couple of Ford’s knaves, his hinds, were called forth by their mistress to carry me in the name of foul clothes to Datchet Lane. They took me on their shoulders, met the jealous knave their master in the door, who asked them once or twice what they had in their basket. I quaked for fear lest the lunatic knave would have searched it; but Fate, ordaining he should be a cuckold, held his hand. Well, on went he for a search, and away went I for foul clothes. But mark the sequel, Master Brook. I suffered the pangs of three several deaths: first, an intolerable fright to be detected with a jealous rotten bell-wether; next, to be compassed like a good bilbo in the circumference of a peck, hilt to point, heel to head; and then, to be stopped in, like a strong distillation, with stinking clothes that fretted in their own grease. Think of that, a man of my kidney, think of that—that am as subject to heat as butter; a man of continual dissolution and thaw. It was a miracle to ’scape suffocation. And in the height of this bath, when I was more than half stewed in grease, like a Dutch dish, to be thrown into the Thames and cooled, glowing hot, in that surge, like a horseshoe! Think of that—hissing hot—think of that, Master Brook.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: In good sadness, sir, I am sorry that for my sake you have suffered all this. My suit, then, is desperate. You’ll undertake her no more?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Master Brook, I will be thrown into Etna, as I have been into Thames, ere I will leave her thus. Her husband is this morning gone a-birding; I have received from her another embassy of meeting. ’Twixt eight and nine is the hour, Master Brook.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: ’Tis past eight already, sir.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Is it? I will then address me to my appointment. Come to me at your convenient leisure, and you shall know how I speed; and the conclusion shall be crowned with your enjoying her. Adieu. You shall have her, Master Brook. Master Brook, you shall cuckold Ford.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Hum! Ha! Is this a vision? Is this a dream? Do I sleep? Master Ford, awake; awake, Master Ford! There’s a hole made in your best coat, Master Ford. This ’tis to be married; this ’tis to have linen and buck-baskets! Well, I will proclaim myself what I am. I will now take the lecher. He is at my house. He cannot scape me. ’Tis impossible he should. He cannot creep into a half-penny purse, nor into a pepperbox. But, lest the devil that guides him should aid him, I will search impossible places. Though what I am I cannot avoid, yet to be what I would not shall not make me tame. If I have horns to make one mad, let the proverb go with me: I’ll be horn-mad.

div.head: ACT IV
SCENE I. The street
div.stage: Enter Mistress Page, Mistress Quickly and William.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Is he at Master Ford’s already, think’st thou?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Sure he is by this; or will be presently. But truly he is very courageous mad about his throwing into the water. Mistress Ford desires you to come suddenly.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: I’ll be with her by and by. I’ll but bring my young man here to school. Look where his master comes; ’tis a playing day, I see.

div.p: How now, Sir Hugh, no school today?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: No, Master Slender is let the boys leave to play.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Blessing of his heart!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Sir Hugh, my husband says my son profits nothing in the world at his book. I pray you ask him some questions in his accidence.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Come hither, William. Hold up your head, come.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Come on, sirrah. Hold up your head. Answer your master, be not afraid.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: William, how many numbers is in nouns?

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: Two.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Truly, I thought there had been one number more, because they say “’Od’s nouns.”

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Peace your tattlings! What is “fair,” William?

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: Pulcher.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Polecats? There are fairer things than polecats, sure.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: You are a very simplicity ’oman; I pray you, peace.—What is lapis, William?

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: A stone.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: And what is “a stone,” William?

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: A pebble.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: No, it is lapis. I pray you remember in your prain.

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: Lapis.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: That is a good William. What is he, William, that does lend articles?

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: Articles are borrowed of the pronoun, and be thus declined: singulariter, nominativo, hic, haec, hoc.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Nominativo, hig, haeg, hog, pray you, mark: genitivo, huius. Well, what is your accusative case?

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: Accusativo, hinc.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: I pray you, have your remembrance, child. Accusativo, hung, hang, hog.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: “Hang-hog” is Latin for bacon, I warrant you.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Leave your prabbles, ’oman.—What is the focative case, William?

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: O—vocativo—O—

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Remember, William; focative is caret.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: And that’s a good root.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: ’Oman, forbear.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Peace.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: What is your genitive case plural, William?

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: Genitive case?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Ay.

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: Genitive: horum, harum, horum.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Vengeance of Jenny’s case, fie on her! Never name her, child, if she be a whore.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: For shame, ’oman.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: You do ill to teach the child such words.—He teaches him to hick and to hack, which they’ll do fast enough of themselves; and to call “whore ’m”!—Fie upon you!

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: ’Oman, art thou lunatics? Hast thou no understandings for thy cases, and the numbers of the genders? Thou art as foolish Christian creatures as I would desires.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: To Quickly. Prithee, hold thy peace.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Show me now, William, some declensions of your pronouns.

sp.speaker: WILLIAM
sp.p: Forsooth, I have forgot.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: It is qui, quae, quod. If you forget your quis, your quaes, and your quods, you must be preeches. Go your ways and play, go.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: He is a better scholar than I thought he was.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: He is a good sprag memory. Farewell, Mistress Page.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Adieu, good Sir Hugh.

div.p: Get you home, boy. Come, we stay too long.

div.head: SCENE II. A room in Ford’s house

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Mistress Ford, your sorrow hath eaten up my sufferance. I see you are obsequious in your love, and I profess requital to a hair’s breadth, not only, Mistress Ford, in the simple office of love, but in all the accoutrement, compliment, and ceremony of it. But are you sure of your husband now?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: He’s a-birding, sweet Sir John.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Within. What ho, gossip Ford, what ho!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Step into the chamber, Sir John.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: How now, sweetheart, who’s at home besides yourself?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Why, none but mine own people.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Indeed?

lg.l: No, certainly.
Aside to her. Speak louder.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Truly, I am so glad you have nobody here.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Why?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Why, woman, your husband is in his old lunes again. He so takes on yonder with my husband, so rails against all married mankind, so curses all Eve’s daughters, of what complexion soever, and so buffets himself on the forehead, crying “Peer out, peer out!” that any madness I ever yet beheld seemed but tameness, civility, and patience, to this his distemper he is in now. I am glad the fat knight is not here.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Why, does he talk of him?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Of none but him, and swears he was carried out, the last time he searched for him, in a basket; protests to my husband he is now here; and hath drawn him and the rest of their company from their sport, to make another experiment of his suspicion. But I am glad the knight is not here. Now he shall see his own foolery.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: How near is he, Mistress Page?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Hard by, at street end. He will be here anon.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I am undone! The knight is here.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Why, then, you are utterly shamed, and he’s but a dead man. What a woman are you! Away with him, away with him! Better shame than murder.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Which way should he go? How should I bestow him? Shall I put him into the basket again?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: No, I’ll come no more i’ the basket. May I not go out ere he come?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Alas, three of Master Ford’s brothers watch the door with pistols, that none shall issue out, otherwise you might slip away ere he came. But what make you here?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: What shall I do? I’ll creep up into the chimney.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: There they always use to discharge their birding-pieces.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Creep into the kiln-hole.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Where is it?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: He will seek there, on my word. Neither press, coffer, chest, trunk, well, vault, but he hath an abstract for the remembrance of such places, and goes to them by his note. There is no hiding you in the house.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I’ll go out then.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: If you go out in your own semblance, you die, Sir John—unless you go out disguised.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: How might we disguise him?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Alas the day, I know not. There is no woman’s gown big enough for him; otherwise he might put on a hat, a muffler, and a kerchief, and so escape.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Good hearts, devise something. Any extremity rather than a mischief.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: My maid’s aunt, the fat woman of Brentford, has a gown above.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: On my word, it will serve him. She’s as big as he is. And there’s her thrummed hat, and her muffler too.—Run up, Sir John.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Go, go, sweet Sir John. Mistress Page and I will look some linen for your head.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Quick, quick! We’ll come dress you straight; put on the gown the while.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I would my husband would meet him in this shape. He cannot abide the old woman of Brentford; he swears she’s a witch, forbade her my house, and hath threatened to beat her.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Heaven guide him to thy husband’s cudgel and the devil guide his cudgel afterwards!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: But is my husband coming?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Ay, in good sadness is he, and talks of the basket too, howsoever he hath had intelligence.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: We’ll try that; for I’ll appoint my men to carry the basket again, to meet him at the door with it as they did last time.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Nay, but he’ll be here presently. Let’s go dress him like the witch of Brentford.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I’ll first direct my men what they shall do with the basket. Go up, I’ll bring linen for him straight.

lg.l: Hang him, dishonest varlet! We cannot misuse him enough.
We’ll leave a proof, by that which we will do,
Wives may be merry and yet honest too.
We do not act that often jest and laugh;
’Tis old but true: “Still swine eats all the draff.”

div.stage: Enter Mistress Ford with John and Robert.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Go, sirs, take the basket again on your shoulders. Your master is hard at door; if he bid you set it down, obey him. Quickly, dispatch.

sp.speaker: JOHN
sp.p: Come, come, take it up.

sp.speaker: ROBERT
sp.p: Pray heaven it be not full of knight again.

sp.speaker: JOHN
sp.p: I hope not, I had lief as bear so much lead.

div.stage: Enter Ford, Page, Shallow, Caius and Sir Hugh Evans.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Ay, but if it prove true, Master Page, have you any way then to unfool me again?—Set down the basket, villain! Somebody call my wife. Youth in a basket! O you panderly rascals! There’s a knot, a gin, a pack, a conspiracy against me. Now shall the devil be shamed.—What, wife, I say! Come, come forth! Behold what honest clothes you send forth to bleaching!

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Why, this passes, Master Ford! You are not to go loose any longer; you must be pinioned.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Why, this is lunatics, this is mad as a mad dog.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: Indeed, Master Ford, this is not well, indeed.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: So say I too, sir.

div.p: Come hither, Mistress Ford—Mistress Ford, the honest woman, the modest wife, the virtuous creature, that hath the jealous fool to her husband! I suspect without cause, mistress, do I?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Heaven be my witness you do, if you suspect me in any dishonesty.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Well said, brazen-face, hold it out.—Come forth, sirrah.

div.stage: Pulls clothes out of the basket.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: This passes.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Are you not ashamed? Let the clothes alone.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I shall find you anon.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: ’Tis unreasonable. Will you take up your wife’s clothes? Come, away.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Empty the basket, I say.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Why, man, why?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Master Page, as I am a man, there was one conveyed out of my house yesterday in this basket. Why may not he be there again? In my house I am sure he is. My intelligence is true, my jealousy is reasonable.—Pluck me out all the linen.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: If you find a man there, he shall die a flea’s death.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Here’s no man.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: By my fidelity, this is not well, Master Ford, this wrongs you.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Master Ford, you must pray, and not follow the imaginations of your own heart. This is jealousies.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Well, he’s not here I seek for.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: No, nor nowhere else but in your brain.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Help to search my house this one time. If I find not what I seek, show no colour for my extremity, let me for ever be your table-sport. Let them say of me “As jealous as Ford, that searched a hollow walnut for his wife’s leman.” Satisfy me once more, once more search with me.

div.stage: Exeunt John and Robert with the basket.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: What, ho, Mistress Page! Come you and the old woman down; my husband will come into the chamber.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Old woman? What old woman’s that?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Why, it is my maid’s aunt of Brentford.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: A witch, a quean, an old cozening quean! Have I not forbid her my house? She comes of errands, does she? We are simple men; we do not know what’s brought to pass under the profession of fortune-telling. She works by charms, by spells, by the figure, and such daubery as this is, beyond our element. We know nothing.—Come down, you witch, you hag, you! Come down, I say!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Nay, good sweet husband!—Good gentlemen, let him not strike the old woman.

div.stage: Enter Falstaff disguised as an old woman, led by Mistress Page.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Come, Mother Prat; come, give me your hand.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I’ll prat her. Beats him. Out of my door, you witch, you rag, you baggage, you polecat, you runnion! Out, out! I’ll conjure you, I’ll fortune-tell you.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Are you not ashamed? I think you have killed the poor woman.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Nay, he will do it. ’Tis a goodly credit for you.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Hang her, witch!

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: By yea and no, I think the ’oman is a witch indeed. I like not when a ’oman has a great peard. I spy a great peard under her muffler.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Will you follow, gentlemen? I beseech you follow, see but the issue of my jealousy. If I cry out thus upon no trail, never trust me when I open again.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Let’s obey his humour a little further. Come, gentlemen.

div.stage: Exeunt Ford, Page, Caius, Evans and Shallow.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Trust me, he beat him most pitifully.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Nay, by th’ mass, that he did not; he beat him most unpitifully, methought.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: I’ll have the cudgel hallowed and hung o’er the altar. It hath done meritorious service.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: What think you? May we, with the warrant of womanhood and the witness of a good conscience, pursue him with any further revenge?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: The spirit of wantonness is sure scared out of him. If the devil have him not in fee-simple, with fine and recovery, he will never, I think, in the way of waste, attempt us again.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Shall we tell our husbands how we have served him?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Yes, by all means, if it be but to scrape the figures out of your husband’s brains. If they can find in their hearts the poor unvirtuous fat knight shall be any further afflicted, we two will still be the ministers.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: I’ll warrant they’ll have him publicly shamed, and methinks there would be no period to the jest should he not be publicly shamed.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Come, to the forge with it, then shape it. I would not have things cool.

div.head: SCENE III. A room in the Garter Inn

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Sir, the Germans desire to have three of your horses. The Duke himself will be tomorrow at court, and they are going to meet him.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: What duke should that be comes so secretly? I hear not of him in the court. Let me speak with the gentlemen. They speak English?

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Ay, sir. I’ll call them to you.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: They shall have my horses, but I’ll make them pay, I’ll sauce them. They have had my house a week at command; I have turned away my other guests. They must come off, I’ll sauce them. Come.

div.head: SCENE IV. A room in Ford’s house
div.stage: Enter Page, Ford, Mistress Page, Mistress Ford and Sir Hugh Evans.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: ’Tis one of the best discretions of a ’oman as ever I did look upon.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: And did he send you both these letters at an instant?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Within a quarter of an hour.

lg.l: Pardon me, wife. Henceforth, do what thou wilt.
I rather will suspect the sun with cold
Than thee with wantonness. Now doth thy honour stand,
In him that was of late an heretic,
As firm as faith.
’Tis well, ’tis well, no more.
Be not as extreme in submission as in offence.
But let our plot go forward. Let our wives
Yet once again, to make us public sport,
Appoint a meeting with this old fat fellow,
Where we may take him and disgrace him for it.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: There is no better way than that they spoke of.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: How? To send him word they’ll meet him in the park at midnight? Fie, fie, he’ll never come.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: You say he has been thrown in the rivers, and has been grievously peaten as an old ’oman. Methinks there should be terrors in him, that he should not come. Methinks his flesh is punished; he shall have no desires.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: So think I too.

lg.l: Devise but how you’ll use him when he comes,
And let us two devise to bring him thither.
There is an old tale goes that Herne the hunter,
Sometime a keeper here in Windsor Forest,
Doth all the winter time, at still midnight,
Walk round about an oak, with great ragged horns,
And there he blasts the tree, and takes the cattle,
And makes milch-kine yield blood, and shakes a chain
In a most hideous and dreadful manner.
You have heard of such a spirit, and well you know
The superstitious idle-headed eld
Received and did deliver to our age,
This tale of Herne the hunter for a truth.
Why, yet there want not many that do fear
In deep of night to walk by this Herne’s oak.
But what of this?
Marry, this is our device,
That Falstaff at that oak shall meet with us,
Disguised like Herne, with huge horns on his head.
Well, let it not be doubted but he’ll come,
And in this shape; when you have brought him thither,
What shall be done with him? What is your plot?
That likewise have we thought upon, and thus:
Nan Page my daughter, and my little son,
And three or four more of their growth, we’ll dress
Like urchins, oafs and fairies, green and white,
With rounds of waxen tapers on their heads
And rattles in their hands. Upon a sudden,
As Falstaff, she, and I are newly met,
Let them from forth a sawpit rush at once
With some diffused song; upon their sight
We two in great amazedness will fly.
Then let them all encircle him about,
And fairy-like, to pinch the unclean knight,
And ask him why, that hour of fairy revel,
In their so sacred paths he dares to tread
In shape profane.
And till he tell the truth,
Let the supposed fairies pinch him sound
And burn him with their tapers.
The truth being known,
We’ll all present ourselves, dis-horn the spirit,
And mock him home to Windsor.
The children must
Be practised well to this, or they’ll ne’er do ’t.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: I will teach the children their behaviours, and I will be like a jackanapes also, to burn the knight with my taber.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: That will be excellent. I’ll go buy them vizards.

lg.l: My Nan shall be the queen of all the fairies,
Finely attired in a robe of white.
That silk will I go buy.
Aside. And in that time
Shall Master Slender steal my Nan away,
And marry her at Eton.—Go, send to Falstaff straight.
Nay, I’ll to him again in name of Brook.
He’ll tell me all his purpose. Sure, he’ll come.
Fear not you that. Go, get us properties
And tricking for our fairies.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Let us about it. It is admirable pleasures and fery honest knaveries.

lg.l: Go, Mistress Ford.
Send quickly to Sir John to know his mind.

div.p: I’ll to the Doctor. He hath my good will, And none but he, to marry with Nan Page. That Slender, though well landed, is an idiot, And he my husband best of all affects. The Doctor is well moneyed, and his friends Potent at court. He, none but he, shall have her, Though twenty thousand worthier come to crave her.

div.head: SCENE V. A room in the Garter Inn

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: What wouldst thou have, boor? What, thick-skin? Speak, breathe, discuss; brief, short, quick, snap.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Marry, sir, I come to speak with Sir John Falstaff from Master Slender.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: There’s his chamber, his house, his castle, his standing-bed and truckle-bed. ’Tis painted about with the story of the Prodigal, fresh and new. Go, knock and call. He’ll speak like an Anthropophaginian unto thee. Knock, I say.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: There’s an old woman, a fat woman, gone up into his chamber. I’ll be so bold as stay, sir, till she come down. I come to speak with her, indeed.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Ha? A fat woman? The knight may be robbed. I’ll call.—Bully knight! Bully Sir John! Speak from thy lungs military. Art thou there? It is thine host, thine Ephesian, calls.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Above. How now, mine host?

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Here’s a Bohemian-Tartar tarries the coming down of thy fat woman. Let her descend, bully, let her descend. My chambers are honourable. Fie! Privacy? Fie!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: There was, mine host, an old fat woman even now with me, but she’s gone.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Pray you, sir, was’t not the wise woman of Brentford?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Ay, marry was it, mussel-shell. What would you with her?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: My master, sir, my Master Slender, sent to her, seeing her go through the streets, to know, sir, whether one Nym, sir, that beguiled him of a chain, had the chain or no.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I spake with the old woman about it.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: And what says she, I pray, sir?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Marry, she says that the very same man that beguiled Master Slender of his chain cozened him of it.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: I would I could have spoken with the woman herself. I had other things to have spoken with her too, from him.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: What are they? Let us know.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Ay, come. Quick.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: I may not conceal them, sir.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Conceal them, or thou diest.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: Why, sir, they were nothing but about Mistress Anne Page, to know if it were my master’s fortune to have her or no.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: ’Tis, ’tis his fortune.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: What sir?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: To have her, or no. Go, say the woman told me so.

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: May I be bold to say so, sir?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Ay, sir; like who more bold?

sp.speaker: SIMPLE
sp.p: I thank your worship; I shall make my master glad with these tidings.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Thou art clerkly, thou art clerkly, Sir John. Was there a wise woman with thee?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Ay, that there was, mine host; one that hath taught me more wit than ever I learned before in my life; and I paid nothing for it neither, but was paid for my learning.

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Out, alas, sir, cozenage, mere cozenage!

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Where be my horses? Speak well of them, varletto.

sp.speaker: BARDOLPH
sp.p: Run away, with the cozeners. For so soon as I came beyond Eton, they threw me off from behind one of them, in a slough of mire, and set spurs and away, like three German devils, three Doctor Faustuses.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: They are gone but to meet the Duke, villain, do not say they be fled. Germans are honest men.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Where is mine host?

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: What is the matter, sir?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Have a care of your entertainments. There is a friend of mine come to town tells me there is three cozen-Germans that has cozened all the hosts of Readings, of Maidenhead, of Colebrook, of horses and money. I tell you for good will, look you. You are wise, and full of gibes and vlouting-stocks, and ’tis not convenient you should be cozened. Fare you well.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Vere is mine host de Jarteer?

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Here, Master Doctor, in perplexity and doubtful dilemma.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: I cannot tell vat is dat, but it is tell-a me dat you make grand preparation for a Duke de Jamany. By my trot, dere is no duke that the court is know to come. I tell you for good will. Adieu.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Hue and cry, villain, go!—Assist me, knight, I am undone.—Fly, run, hue and cry, villain, I am undone!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I would all the world might be cozened, for I have been cozened and beaten too. If it should come to the ear of the court how I have been transformed, and how my transformation hath been washed and cudgelled, they would melt me out of my fat drop by drop, and liquor fishermen’s boots with me. I warrant they would whip me with their fine wits till I were as crestfallen as a dried pear. I never prospered since I forswore myself at primero. Well, if my wind were but long enough, I would repent.

div.p: Now, whence come you?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: From the two parties, forsooth.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: The devil take one party and his dam the other, and so they shall be both bestowed. I have suffered more for their sakes, more than the villainous inconstancy of man’s disposition is able to bear.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: And have not they suffered? Yes, I warrant, speciously one of them. Mistress Ford, good heart, is beaten black and blue, that you cannot see a white spot about her.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: What tellst thou me of black and blue? I was beaten myself into all the colours of the rainbow, and was like to be apprehended for the witch of Brentford. But that my admirable dexterity of wit, my counterfeiting the action of an old woman, delivered me, the knave constable had set me i’ the stocks, i’ the common stocks, for a witch.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: Sir, let me speak with you in your chamber, you shall hear how things go, and, I warrant, to your content. Here is a letter will say somewhat. Good hearts, what ado here is to bring you together! Sure, one of you does not serve heaven well, that you are so crossed.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Come up into my chamber.

div.head: SCENE VI. Another room in the Garter Inn

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Master Fenton, talk not to me. My mind is heavy. I will give over all.

lg.l: Yet hear me speak. Assist me in my purpose,
And, as I am a gentleman, I’ll give thee
A hundred pound in gold more than your loss.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: I will hear you, Master Fenton, and I will, at the least, keep your counsel.

lg.l: From time to time I have acquainted you
With the dear love I bear to fair Anne Page,
Who mutually hath answered my affection,
So far forth as herself might be her chooser,
Even to my wish. I have a letter from her
Of such contents as you will wonder at,
The mirth whereof so larded with my matter
That neither singly can be manifested
Without the show of both, wherein fat Falstaff
Hath a great scene; the image of the jest
I’ll show you here at large. Hark, good mine host:
Tonight at Herne’s oak, just ’twixt twelve and one,
Must my sweet Nan present the Fairy Queen—
The purpose why is here—in which disguise,
While other jests are something rank on foot,
Her father hath commanded her to slip
Away with Slender, and with him at Eton
Immediately to marry. She hath consented. Now, sir,
Her mother, even strong against that match
And firm for Doctor Caius, hath appointed
That he shall likewise shuffle her away,
While other sports are tasking of their minds,
And at the dean’ry, where a priest attends,
Straight marry her. To this her mother’s plot
She, seemingly obedient, likewise hath
Made promise to the doctor. Now thus it rests:
Her father means she shall be all in white
And in that habit, when Slender sees his time
To take her by the hand and bid her go,
She shall go with him. Her mother hath intended
The better to denote her to the doctor,
For they must all be masked and vizarded—
That quaint in green she shall be loose enrobed,
With ribbons pendant flaring ’bout her head;
And when the doctor spies his vantage ripe,
To pinch her by the hand, and on that token
The maid hath given consent to go with him.

sp.speaker: HOST
sp.p: Which means she to deceive, father or mother?

lg.l: Both, my good host, to go along with me.
And here it rests, that you’ll procure the vicar
To stay for me at church, ’twixt twelve and one,
And, in the lawful name of marrying,
To give our hearts united ceremony.
Well, husband your device; I’ll to the vicar.
Bring you the maid, you shall not lack a priest.
So shall I evermore be bound to thee;
Besides, I’ll make a present recompense.

div.head: ACT V
SCENE I. A room in the Garter Inn

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Prithee, no more prattling. Go. I’ll hold. This is the third time; I hope good luck lies in odd numbers. Away, go! They say there is divinity in odd numbers, either in nativity, chance, or death. Away!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
sp.p: I’ll provide you a chain, and I’ll do what I can to get you a pair of horns.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Away, I say; time wears. Hold up your head, and mince.

div.p: How now, Master Brook! Master Brook, the matter will be known tonight or never. Be you in the park about midnight, at Herne’s oak, and you shall see wonders.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Went you not to her yesterday, sir, as you told me you had appointed?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I went to her, Master Brook, as you see, like a poor old man, but I came from her, Master Brook, like a poor old woman. That same knave Ford, her husband, hath the finest mad devil of jealousy in him, Master Brook, that ever governed frenzy. I will tell you he beat me grievously, in the shape of a woman; for in the shape of man, Master Brook, I fear not Goliath with a weaver’s beam, because I know also life is a shuttle. I am in haste. Go along with me; I’ll tell you all, Master Brook. Since I plucked geese, played truant, and whipped top, I knew not what ’twas to be beaten till lately. Follow me, I’ll tell you strange things of this knave Ford, on whom tonight I will be revenged, and I will deliver his wife into your hand. Follow. Strange things in hand, Master Brook! Follow.

div.head: SCENE II. Windsor Park

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Come, come. We’ll couch i’ the castle ditch till we see the light of our fairies. Remember, son Slender, my daughter—

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Ay, forsooth. I have spoke with her, and we have a nay-word how to know one another. I come to her in white and cry “mum”; she cries “budget”; and by that we know one another.

sp.speaker: SHALLOW
sp.p: That’s good too. But what needs either your “mum” or her “budget”? The white will decipher her well enough. It hath struck ten o’clock.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: The night is dark. Light and spirits will become it well. Heaven prosper our sport! No man means evil but the devil, and we shall know him by his horns. Let’s away; follow me.

div.head: SCENE III. The street in Windsor
div.stage: Enter Mistress Page, Mistress Ford and Doctor Caius.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Master Doctor, my daughter is in green. When you see your time, take her by the hand, away with her to the deanery, and dispatch it quickly. Go before into the park. We two must go together.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: I know vat I have to do. Adieu.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Fare you well, sir.

div.p: My husband will not rejoice so much at the abuse of Falstaff as he will chafe at the doctor’s marrying my daughter. But ’tis no matter. Better a little chiding than a great deal of heartbreak.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Where is Nan now, and her troop of fairies, and the Welsh devil Hugh?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: They are all couched in a pit hard by Herne’s oak, with obscured lights, which, at the very instant of Falstaff’s and our meeting, they will at once display to the night.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: That cannot choose but amaze him.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: If he be not amazed, he will be mocked; if he be amazed, he will every way be mocked.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: We’ll betray him finely.

lg.l: Against such lewdsters and their lechery,
Those that betray them do no treachery.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: The hour draws on. To the oak, to the oak!

div.head: SCENE IV. Windsor Park
div.stage: Enter Sir Hugh Evans disguised, and children as Fairies.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Trib, trib, fairies. Come, and remember your parts. Be pold, I pray you, follow me into the pit, and when I give the watch-’ords, do as I pid you. Come, come; trib, trib.

div.head: SCENE V. Another part of the Park
div.stage: Enter Falstaff wearing a buck’s head.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: The Windsor bell hath struck twelve, the minute draws on. Now the hot-blooded gods assist me! Remember, Jove, thou wast a bull for thy Europa; love set on thy horns. O powerful love, that in some respects, makes a beast a man, in some other a man a beast! You were also, Jupiter, a swan for the love of Leda. O omnipotent love, how near the god drew to the complexion of a goose! A fault done first in the form of a beast; O Jove, a beastly fault! And then another fault in the semblance of a fowl; think on’t, Jove, a foul fault! When gods have hot backs, what shall poor men do? For me, I am here a Windsor stag, and the fattest, I think, i’ the forest. Send me a cool rut-time, Jove, or who can blame me to piss my tallow? Who comes here? My doe?

div.stage: Enter Mistress Ford and Mistress Page.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Sir John? Art thou there, my deer, my male deer?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: My doe with the black scut! Let the sky rain potatoes, let it thunder to the tune of “Greensleeves”, hail kissing-comfits and snow eringoes; let there come a tempest of provocation, I will shelter me here.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Mistress Page is come with me, sweetheart.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Divide me like a bribed buck, each a haunch. I will keep my sides to myself, my shoulders for the fellow of this walk, and my horns I bequeath your husbands. Am I a woodman, ha? Speak I like Herne the hunter? Why, now is Cupid a child of conscience; he makes restitution. As I am a true spirit, welcome!

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Alas, what noise?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Heaven forgive our sins!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: What should this be?

div.p: MISTRESS FORD and MISTRESS PAGE. Away, away!

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I think the devil will not have me damned, lest the oil that’s in me should set hell on fire; he would never else cross me thus.

div.stage: Enter Mistress Quickly as the Queen of Fairies, Sir Hugh Evans as a Satyr, Pistol as Hobgoblin, Anne Page and children as Fairies, carrying tapers.

lg.l: Fairies, black, grey, green, and white,
You moonshine revellers and shades of night,
You orphan heirs of fixed destiny,
Attend your office and your quality.
Crier Hobgoblin, make the fairy oyes.
Elves, list your names; silence, you airy toys!
Cricket, to Windsor chimneys shalt thou leap,
Where fires thou find’st unraked and hearths unswept,
There pinch the maids as blue as bilberry.
Our radiant queen hates sluts and sluttery.
They are fairies, he that speaks to them shall die.
I’ll wink and couch. No man their works must eye.
Where’s Bead? Go you, and where you find a maid
That ere she sleep has thrice her prayers said,
Rein up the organs of her fantasy;
Sleep she as sound as careless infancy.
But those as sleep and think not on their sins,
Pinch them, arms, legs, backs, shoulders, sides, and shins.
About, about!
Search Windsor castle, elves, within and out.
Strew good luck, oafs, on every sacred room,
That it may stand till the perpetual doom
In state as wholesome as in state ’tis fit,
Worthy the owner and the owner it.
The several chairs of order look you scour
With juice of balm and every precious flower.
Each fair instalment, coat, and several crest,
With loyal blazon, evermore be blest!
And nightly, meadow-fairies, look you sing,
Like to the Garter’s compass, in a ring.
Th’ expressure that it bears, green let it be,
More fertile-fresh than all the field to see;
And Honi soit qui mal y pense write
In em’rald tufts, flowers purple, blue and white,
Like sapphire, pearl, and rich embroidery,
Buckled below fair knighthood’s bending knee.
Fairies use flowers for their charactery.
Away, disperse! But till ’tis one o’clock,
Our dance of custom round about the oak
Of Herne the hunter let us not forget.
Pray you, lock hand in hand, yourselves in order set;
And twenty glow-worms shall our lanterns be,
To guide our measure round about the tree.
But stay, I smell a man of middle earth.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Heavens defend me from that Welsh fairy, lest he transform me to a piece of cheese!

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: Vile worm, thou wast o’erlooked even in thy birth.

lg.l: With trial-fire touch me his finger-end.
If he be chaste, the flame will back descend
And turn him to no pain; but if he start,
It is the flesh of a corrupted heart.

sp.speaker: PISTOL
sp.p: A trial, come.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Come, will this wood take fire?

div.stage: They put the tapers to his fingers, and he starts.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: O, o, o!

lg.l: Corrupt, corrupt, and tainted in desire!
About him, fairies, sing a scornful rhyme,
And, as you trip, still pinch him to your time.
Fie on sinful fantasy!
Fie on lust and luxury!
Lust is but a bloody fire,
Kindled with unchaste desire,
Fed in heart, whose flames aspire,
As thoughts do blow them, higher and higher.
Pinch him, fairies, mutually;
Pinch him for his villainy.
Pinch him and burn him and turn him about,
Till candles and starlight and moonshine be out.

div.stage: During the song they pinch him, and Doctor Caius comes one way and steals away a boy in green; and Slender another way takes a boy in white; Fenton comes in and steals away Anne Page. A noise of hunting is heard within and all the fairies run away. Falstaff pulls off his buck’s head, and rises up.
Enter Page, Ford, Mistress Page and Mistress Ford.

lg.l: Nay, do not fly. I think we have watched you now.
Will none but Herne the hunter serve your turn?
I pray you, come, hold up the jest no higher.—
Now, good Sir John, how like you Windsor wives?
See you these, husband?

div.p: Do not these fair yokes Become the forest better than the town?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Now, sir, who’s a cuckold now? Master Brook, Falstaff’s a knave, a cuckoldly knave. Here are his horns, Master Brook. And, Master Brook, he hath enjoyed nothing of Ford’s but his buck-basket, his cudgel, and twenty pounds of money, which must be paid to Master Brook. His horses are arrested for it, Master Brook.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS FORD
sp.p: Sir John, we have had ill luck, we could never meet. I will never take you for my love again, but I will always count you my deer.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I do begin to perceive that I am made an ass.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Ay, and an ox too. Both the proofs are extant.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: And these are not fairies? I was three or four times in the thought they were not fairies; and yet the guiltiness of my mind, the sudden surprise of my powers, drove the grossness of the foppery into a received belief, in despite of the teeth of all rhyme and reason, that they were fairies. See now how wit may be made a Jack-a-Lent when ’tis upon ill employment!

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Sir John Falstaff, serve Got, and leave your desires, and fairies will not pinse you.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Well said, fairy Hugh.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: And leave you your jealousies too, I pray you.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: I will never mistrust my wife again, till thou art able to woo her in good English.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Have I laid my brain in the sun, and dried it, that it wants matter to prevent so gross o’erreaching as this? Am I ridden with a Welsh goat too? Shall I have a cox-comb of frieze? ’Tis time I were choked with a piece of toasted cheese.

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: Seese is not good to give putter. Your belly is all putter.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: “Seese” and “putter”? Have I lived to stand at the taunt of one that makes fritters of English? This is enough to be the decay of lust and late-walking through the realm.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Why, Sir John, do you think, though we would have thrust virtue out of our hearts by the head and shoulders, and have given ourselves without scruple to hell, that ever the devil could have made you our delight?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: What, a hodge-pudding? A bag of flax?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: A puffed man?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Old, cold, withered, and of intolerable entrails?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: And one that is as slanderous as Satan?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: And as poor as Job?

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: And as wicked as his wife?

sp.speaker: EVANS
sp.p: And given to fornications, and to taverns, and sack, and wine, and metheglins, and to drinkings and swearings and starings, pribbles and prabbles?

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: Well, I am your theme. You have the start of me. I am dejected, I am not able to answer the Welsh flannel. Ignorance itself is a plummet o’er me. Use me as you will.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: Marry, sir, we’ll bring you to Windsor to one Master Brook, that you have cozened of money, to whom you should have been a pander. Over and above that you have suffered, I think to repay that money will be a biting affliction.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Yet be cheerful, knight. Thou shalt eat a posset tonight at my house, where I will desire thee to laugh at my wife, that now laughs at thee. Tell her Master Slender hath married her daughter.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Aside. Doctors doubt that. If Anne Page be my daughter, she is, by this, Doctor Caius’ wife.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Whoa, ho, ho, father Page!

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Son, how now! How now, son, have you dispatched?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: Dispatched? I’ll make the best in Gloucestershire know on’t. Would I were hanged, la, else!

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Of what, son?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I came yonder at Eton to marry Mistress Anne Page, and she’s a great lubberly boy. If it had not been i’ the church, I would have swinged him, or he should have swinged me. If I did not think it had been Anne Page, would I might never stir! And ’tis a postmaster’s boy.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Upon my life, then, you took the wrong.

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: What need you tell me that? I think so, when I took a boy for a girl. If I had been married to him, for all he was in woman’s apparel, I would not have had him.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Why, this is your own folly. Did not I tell you how you should know my daughter by her garments?

sp.speaker: SLENDER
sp.p: I went to her in white and cried “mum”, and she cried “budget”, as Anne and I had appointed, and yet it was not Anne, but a postmaster’s boy.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Good George, be not angry. I knew of your purpose, turned my daughter into green, and indeed she is now with the doctor at the deanery, and there married.

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Vere is Mistress Page? By gar, I am cozened, I ha’ married un garçon, a boy; un paysan, by gar, a boy. It is not Anne Page. By gar, I am cozened.

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Why, did you take her in green?

sp.speaker: CAIUS
sp.p: Ay, by gar, and ’tis a boy. By gar, I’ll raise all Windsor.

sp.speaker: FORD
sp.p: This is strange. Who hath got the right Anne?

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: My heart misgives me. Here comes Master Fenton.—How now, Master Fenton!

sp.speaker: ANNE
sp.p: Pardon, good father. Good my mother, pardon.

sp.speaker: PAGE
sp.p: Now, mistress, how chance you went not with Master Slender?

sp.speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
sp.p: Why went you not with Master Doctor, maid?

lg.l: You do amaze her. Hear the truth of it.
You would have married her most shamefully,
Where there was no proportion held in love.
The truth is, she and I, long since contracted,
Are now so sure that nothing can dissolve us.
Th’ offence is holy that she hath committed,
And this deceit loses the name of craft,
Of disobedience, or unduteous title,
Since therein she doth evitate and shun
A thousand irreligious cursed hours,
Which forced marriage would have brought upon her.
Stand not amazed, here is no remedy.
In love, the heavens themselves do guide the state.
Money buys lands, and wives are sold by fate.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: I am glad, though you have ta’en a special stand to strike at me, that your arrow hath glanced.

lg.l: Well, what remedy? Fenton, heaven give thee joy!
What cannot be eschewed must be embraced.

sp.speaker: FALSTAFF
sp.p: When night-dogs run, all sorts of deer are chased.

lg.l: Well, I will muse no further.—Master Fenton,
Heaven give you many, many merry days!
Good husband, let us every one go home,
And laugh this sport o’er by a country fire,
Sir John and all.
Let it be so, Sir John,
To Master Brook you yet shall hold your word,
For he tonight shall lie with Mistress Ford.
